title: 正德五年浙江鄉試錄
text:
浙江鄉□
國家三歲論秀□在今甲
五年實維其期浙江藩
司先事白于巡按監察□
陳鼐祗若
成□悉銳□□□□時鎮守□
監劉璟□□□□□□□旬
===
造太監楊□監舶太監
清戎監察御史李春芳□□
鹽法監察御史邢昭切
賛有事茲土者主事滕□
僉韓邦靖亦相厥美御史
鼐諗於眾曰以人事君在□
道篤忠哉□□□□□忠□
punctuated:
浙江鄉□

國家三歲論秀，□在今甲五年，實維其期。浙江藩司先事白于巡按監察□陳鼐，祗若成□，悉銳□□□□。時鎮守□監劉璟□□□□□□□旬，造太監楊□、監舶太監、清戎監察御史李春芳□□、鹽法監察御史邢昭，切賛。有事茲土者，主事滕□、僉韓邦靖，亦相厥美。御史鼐諗於眾曰：「以人事君，在□道篤忠哉！□□□□□忠□」
translation_en:
Zhejiang Provincial … [title illegible]

Every three years, the state evaluates outstanding talent. [Illegible] in the present jia fifth year [?], the appointed time had indeed arrived. The Zhejiang Provincial Administration Commission reported beforehand to the Regional Inspector, Investigating Censor Chen Nai 陳鼐. Respectfully following the established [illegible], they fully directed their energies toward [illegible; reading uncertain]. At that time, the Regional Defender, Eunuch [?] Liu Jing 劉璟, [illegible passage containing a reference to a ten-day period]; the construction eunuch [?] Yang □; the Eunuch Superintendent of Maritime Trade; Investigating Censor Li Chunfang 李春芳, responsible for inspecting military affairs, [illegible]; and Investigating Censor Xing Zhao 邢昭, responsible for the salt administration, gave earnest assistance. Those serving in this territory—Secretary Teng □ and Assistant Commissioner [?] Han Bangjing 韓邦靖—also helped bring this worthy undertaking to fruition. Censor Nai addressed the assembled officials, saying: “Serving the ruler by providing men of talent lies in [illegible] the Way and being steadfast in loyalty! [Illegible passage containing the word ‘loyalty’] …”

title: 正德五年浙江鄉試錄
text:
古人進賢□□□進也
賢宜蒙重譴矣是弗可弗加
之意於是公會藩臬分遣□
幣擇聘鳴鳳李泰為考□
賈策余廷濟張禎秦□□
王德廣文□洪敏為同考
官戒提學□□簡譽髦副□□
旦始至歷十一郡群而試之
得有藝可入塲屋者二□□
奇至八月朔巡按出□
藩司職提調以屬左布□□
劉琬右參議白圻臬司職監
試以屬按察使邊憲僉事許
朝宗其目□□□□□布□
punctuated: 古人進賢□□□進也，賢宜蒙重譴矣，是弗可弗加之意。於是公會藩臬，分遣□幣，擇聘鳴鳳、李泰為考□，賈策、余廷濟、張禎、秦□□、王德、廣文□洪敏為同考官，戒提學□□簡譽髦。副□□旦始至，歷十一郡，群而試之，得有藝可入塲屋者二□□奇。至八月朔，巡按出□，藩司職提調，以屬左布□□劉琬、右參議白圻；臬司職監試，以屬按察使邊憲、僉事許朝宗。其目□□□□□布□
translation_en:
…The ancients recommended worthy men [illegible] advancement [?]. The worthy ought to incur severe reprimand [?]; this was something to which attention must be given. Accordingly, His Lordship conferred with the provincial administrative and surveillance authorities and dispatched men with [illegible] gifts to engage Mingfeng and Li Tai as Examiners [?], and Jia Ce, Yu Tingji, Zhang Zhen, Qin [two illegible characters], Wang De, and the instructor [illegible] Hong Min [?] as Associate Examiners. He instructed the Education Intendant [illegible] to select outstanding scholars of good reputation. The deputy [illegible] had only just arrived [?]. He traveled through the eleven prefectures, assembling the candidates and examining them, and obtained two [illegible numerical units] and some additional men whose literary attainments qualified them to enter the examination compound.

On the first day of the eighth month, the Regional Inspector issued [illegible]. The Provincial Administration Commission was responsible for the duties of Proctor, which were entrusted to Liu Wan, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner [title partly illegible], and Bai Qi, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner. The Provincial Surveillance Commission was responsible for supervising the examination, which was entrusted to Surveillance Commissioner Bian Xian and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Xu Chaozong. The list [illegible; an official title begins here] …

title: 正德五年浙江鄉試錄
text:
使夏景和□□正作□右參
政黃瓚副使彭澤左參議任
渤右參議陳珀徐瑤僉事□
惟王金楊惟康吳希由□□
都指揮僉事魏文禮□□□
昶陳璠張□楊輅亦與在□
也此外收□試卷則知府楊
孟瑛石存□餘悉選才以充
總統試事□監臨之不□
明不苛而嚴不煩而密□
以貞御史象也七日庚寅
院九日壬辰雞鳴庶正群
咸起將事巡按與藩臬啓篋
偕鳴鳳等□□□□四書
punctuated:
使夏景和□□正作□、右參政黃瓚、副使彭澤、左參議任渤、右參議陳珀、徐瑤、僉事□惟、王金、楊惟康、吳希由□□、都指揮僉事魏文禮□□□昶、陳璠、張□、楊輅，亦與在□也。此外，收□試卷則知府楊孟瑛、石存□，餘悉選才以充。總統試事□監臨之不□，明不苛而嚴，不煩而密，□以貞，御史象也。
七日庚寅，院。九日壬辰，雞鳴，庶正群咸起將事。巡按與藩臬啓篋，偕鳴鳳等□□□□四書
translation_en:
…Commissioner Xia Jinghe [the following text is illegible or garbled: □□正作□]; Right Administration Vice Commissioner Huang Zan; Surveillance Vice Commissioner Peng Ze; Left Administration Assistant Commissioner Ren Bo; Right Administration Assistant Commissioners Chen Po and Xu Yao; Surveillance Assistant Commissioners □ Wei, Wang Jin, Yang Weikang, and Wu Xiyou [two illegible characters]; and Regional Military Assistant Commissioner Wei Wenli, [three illegible characters] Chang, Chen Fan, Zhang □, and Yang Lu also participated in [illegible] [?]. In addition, Prefects Yang Mengying and Shi Cun□ were responsible for collecting [illegible] examination papers. All remaining positions were filled by selecting capable men. Overall direction of examination affairs [illegible] and supervision [text unclear]. Discerning, they maintained strictness without harshness and thoroughness without vexatious interference; [illegible] with steadfastness—such was the censor’s example [?].
On the seventh day, gengyin, [they entered?] the examination compound [?]. On the ninth day, renchen, at cockcrow, the various officials all rose to attend to their duties. The Regional Inspector and the provincial administration and surveillance officials opened the chest and, together with Mingfeng and the others, [four illegible characters] the Four Books…

title: 正德五年浙江鄉試錄
text:
五經刺題□□□□□□附傳
註紬繹經義爭出所聞見以
未將觀其論議試之再戊□
又觀其經畧試之三遵
定額取九十人事竣勒其名
及可程之文爲錄馳獻于
上鳴鳳得叙諸首簡惟浙文獻大
===
藩先正道德文章勛名忠節
炳著百世甞讀陸宣公韓忠
獻公之書判正邪陳利害□
忠悃救時弊下宣民鬱上□
主聰蓋賢相也甞讀許都□
宗忠簡之書畧謀畫展威武
□□應變之
才足以干
punctuated:
五經刺題□□□□□□附傳註，紬繹經義，爭出所聞見，以未將觀其論議，試之再戊□；又觀其經畧，試之三。遵定額，取九十人。事竣，勒其名及可程之文爲錄，馳獻于上。鳴鳳得叙諸首簡。
惟浙文獻大藩，先正道德、文章、勛名、忠節，炳著百世。甞讀陸宣公、韓忠獻公之書，判正邪，陳利害，□忠悃，救時弊，下宣民鬱，上□主聰，蓋賢相也。甞讀許都□、宗忠簡之書，畧謀畫，展威武，□□應變之才，足以干
translation_en:
…questions selected from the Five Classics [?; six illegible characters], drawing on the commentaries and annotations, unraveling the meaning of the classics, and each striving to present what he had heard and seen. The next phrase is unclear [?]. To assess their arguments, they were examined a second time, on wu□ [?]; to assess their capacity for practical governance, they were examined a third time. Following the prescribed quota, ninety men were selected. When the proceedings were complete, their names and essays worthy of serving as models were inscribed in a record and dispatched posthaste for presentation to the Emperor. I, Mingfeng, had the opportunity to write the preface on its opening pages.
Zhejiang is a great province rich in cultural traditions and learned men. The moral virtue, literary achievements, meritorious reputations, loyalty, and integrity of its former worthies shine through a hundred generations. I have read the writings of Lu, Duke Xuan, and Han, Duke Zhongxian. They distinguished right from wrong, set forth advantages and dangers, expressed heartfelt loyalty [?], and remedied the abuses of their times. Below, they gave voice to the people's pent-up grievances; above, they informed the sovereign's understanding [?]. They were indeed worthy chief councillors. I have read the writings of Xu Du□ [?] and Zong Zhongjian: their strategic planning [?], their display of martial prowess, and their ability to respond to changing circumstances [two illegible characters] were sufficient to undertake…

title: 正德五年浙江鄉試錄
text:
匡社稷死生以之者名將也
嘗讀呂東萊何北山諸君子
之書析義淵微履道醇固
孔孟憲濂洛著述滿家皆
儒也嘗讀黃晉卿柳道傳
景濂之書源委宏深論議□
博馳騁百氏根據經史皆大
===
家也是豈無所自哉蓋兩浙
之區盤薄口山綱領完□□
槩雄偉襟帶江海脉絡□□
潮汐洶涌故其高大者發□
為勛名壯銳者發而為忠□
純懿者發而為道德英秀□
發而為文章此□□君子□
punctuated: 匡社稷，死生以之者，名將也。嘗讀呂東萊、何北山諸君子之書，析義淵微，履道醇固，孔孟憲濂洛，著述滿家，皆儒也。嘗讀黃晉卿、柳道傳、景濂之書，源委宏深，論議□博，馳騁百氏，根據經史，皆大家也。是豈無所自哉？蓋兩浙之區，盤薄口山，綱領完□□槩雄偉，襟帶江海，脉絡□□，潮汐洶涌。故其高大者發□為勛名，壯銳者發而為忠□，純懿者發而為道德，英秀□發而為文章。此□□君子□
translation_en:
…those who uphold the altars of soil and grain, devoting themselves to this in life and death, are renowned generals. I have read the writings of such gentlemen as Lü Donglai and He Beishan: their analysis of principles is profound and subtle, and their practice of the Way is pure and steadfast. They follow Confucius and Mencius and take the Lian and Luo traditions as their models [?]; their writings fill their homes. All are Confucian scholars. I have read the writings of Huang Jinqing, Liu Daochuan, and Jinglian: their learning is broad and deep, tracing sources and ramifications; their discussions are […] extensive. They range freely through the hundred schools, grounding themselves in the Classics and histories. All are great masters of letters. Could this possibly have arisen without a source?

The region of Liangzhe spreads expansively amid mountains [?]; its principal mountain chains are whole […] and imposing in aspect [?]. Rivers and the sea encircle it like lapels and a belt; its branching veins […], and its tides surge turbulently. Thus its lofty and vast qualities manifest […] as meritorious achievement and renown; its vigorous and keen qualities manifest as loyalty […]; its pure and excellent qualities manifest as moral virtue; and its brilliant and refined qualities […] manifest as literary accomplishment. These […] gentlemen […]…

title: 正德五年浙江鄉試錄
text:
以靈其地也□□□□無以
往昔肆多士之文雖得之箋
晷有雅意經世思樹勳業如
陸如趙者有植志忠藎因□
節義如許如宗者有析道□
奧志於道□如呂如何者有
含英咀華心於文章如黃如
===
柳如宋者譬之奇珍海蘊山
藏卒不可掩於戲懿哉我
祖宗至今百四十餘年承平重
光岳之氣益完文明之化□
洽人才之出視古滋盛非偶
然也鳴鳳不妄敢以此敘鹿
鳴之宴及揚觶□□具訓之
punctuated: 以靈其地也。□□□□無以往昔。肆多士之文，雖得之箋晷，有雅意經世、思樹勳業如陸如趙者；有植志忠藎、因□節義如許如宗者；有析道□奧、志於道□如呂如何者；有含英咀華、心於文章如黃如柳如宋者。譬之奇珍，海蘊山藏，卒不可掩。於戲，懿哉！我祖宗至今百四十餘年，承平重光，岳之氣益完，文明之化□洽，人才之出視古滋盛，非偶然也。鳴鳳不妄，敢以此敘鹿鳴之宴，及揚觶□□具訓之
translation_en:
…to endow their land with spiritual potency. [Four illegible characters] no means [of comparing with?] former times [?]. Thus, although the writings of these many scholars were obtained on paper within a brief span [?], some reveal lofty aspirations to order the world and establish meritorious achievements, like Lu and Zhao; some reveal a firm commitment to devoted loyalty and to moral integrity and righteousness [partly illegible], like Xu and Zong; some probe the profundities of the Way and aspire to the Way [partly illegible], like Lü and He; and some savor literary excellence and devote their hearts to writing, like Huang, Liu, and Song. They resemble rare treasures stored in the seas and concealed in the mountains: ultimately, they cannot remain hidden. Ah, how splendid!

From the time of our imperial ancestors until now, more than 140 years have passed in peace, with successive renewals of splendor. The vital force of the mountains has grown ever more complete; the transforming influence of civil culture has become [illegible] pervasive. That talented men emerge in greater abundance than in antiquity is no accident. Mingfeng does not speak recklessly and ventures to write this preface for the Deer Cry Banquet and, when raising the ceremonial wine cup, [two illegible characters] to offer full instruction to the…

title: 正德五年浙江鄉試錄
text:
士俾知今日之選雖山川之
靈實賴
聖朝作養宜相與感激而圖報以
逭於媿負也
順天府薊州儒學學正張
鳳謹序
punctuated:
士，俾知今日之選，雖山川之靈，實賴聖朝作養，宜相與感激而圖報，以逭於媿負也。
順天府薊州儒學學正張鳳謹序。
translation_en:
…scholars, so that they may understand that, although their selection today owes something to the numinous influence of mountains and rivers, it truly depends on the nurturing care of the sagely dynasty. They should together feel gratitude and seek to repay this favor, thereby avoiding the shame of failing the trust placed in them.
Preface respectfully composed by Zhang Feng, Instructor of the Confucian School of Jizhou, Shuntian Prefecture.

title: 正德五年浙江鄉試錄
text:

順天府薊州儒學學正張鳴鳳〔□音山東清平縣人丙辰進士〕

河南汝寧府信陽州儒學學正賈策〔廷獻直隸□□□□甲子貢士〕

陝西西安府□□縣儒學教諭□信〔行之山西陵川縣人甲子貢士〕
punctuated:
正德五年浙江鄉試。

監臨官：巡按浙江監察御史陳爕〔汝和，直隸遷安縣人，壬戌進□〕。

提調官：浙江等處承宣布政使司左布政使劉琬〔德資，江西□□□□，戌戌進士〕。浙江等處承宣布政使司右參議白圻〔輔之，直□□□□□，甲辰進士〕。

監試官：浙江等處提刑按察司按察使邊憲〔汝成，直隸任丘縣人，□辰進士〕。浙江等處提刑按察□僉事謝朝宣〔□□，陝西西安左衛籍，直隸臨淮縣人，□□□□〕。

考試官：順天府薊州儒學學正張鳴鳳〔□音，山東清平縣人，丙辰進士〕。陝西臨洮府蘭州儒學學正李泰〔巖夫，河南祥符縣人，甲子貢士〕。

同考試官：河南汝寧府信陽州儒學學正賈策〔廷獻，直隸□□□□，甲子貢士〕。山西遼州儒學學正余廷濟〔仁甫，福建□□□□，甲子貢士〕。河南河南府洛陽縣儒學教諭張禎〔國興，山東章丘□□，丁卯貢士〕。湖廣長沙府湘鄉縣儒學教諭秦鎰〔世用，廣西宜山縣人，辛酉貢士〕。陝西西安府□□縣儒學教諭□信〔行之，山西陵川縣人，甲子貢士〕。
translation_en:
Zhejiang Provincial Examination, fifth year of Zhengde (1510).

Supervising Official:
Chen Xie, Regional Inspector of Zhejiang and Investigating Censor. His courtesy name was Ruhe; he was from Qian’an County, Zhili, and attained the metropolitan graduate degree in the renxu year [final character of the degree designation illegible].

Proctors:
Liu Wan, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Zhejiang. His courtesy name was Dezi; he was from Jiangxi [four characters illegible], and was a metropolitan graduate of the year transcribed as “xuxu” [?].
Bai Qi, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner of Zhejiang. His courtesy name was Fuzhi; his place of origin is recorded as “Zhi…” [five characters illegible]. He was a metropolitan graduate of the jiachen year.

Examination Monitoring Officials:
Bian Xian, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Zhejiang. His courtesy name was Rucheng; he was from Renqiu County, Zhili, and was a metropolitan graduate of the [illegible]-chen year.
Xie Chaoxuan, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of Zhejiang [one character in the agency name is illegible]. His courtesy name is illegible. He was registered in the Xi’an Left Guard, Shaanxi, and was from Linhuai County, Zhili [four following characters illegible].

Examiners:
Zhang Mingfeng, Instructor in the Confucian School of Jizhou, Shuntian Prefecture. His courtesy name was [illegible]-yin; he was from Qingping County, Shandong, and was a metropolitan graduate of the bingchen year.
Li Tai, Instructor in the Confucian School of Lanzhou, Lintao Prefecture, Shaanxi. His courtesy name was Yanfu; he was from Xiangfu County, Henan, and was a tribute student (gongshi) of the jiazi year.

Associate Examiners:
Jia Ce, Instructor in the Confucian School of Xinyang Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan. His courtesy name was Tingxian; he was from Zhili [four characters illegible], and was a tribute student of the jiazi year.

周祜以對于天下
豐年多黍多稂亦有高廩萬億及秭為酒
為醴烝畀祖妣以洽百禮降福孔皆
春秋
公及齊大夫盟于蔇莊公九年九月戊辰
諸侯盟于葵丘僖公九年
夏楚人滅黃僖公十有二年楚人敗徐于
婁林僖公十有五年秋宋公楚子陳
punctuated:
用閔于天越民。公曰：「嗚呼！君惟乃知民德，亦罔不能厥初，惟其終。祗若茲，往敬用治。」
臣人咸若，時惟良顯哉！

詩
無已太康，職思其居。好樂無荒，良士瞿瞿。
樂只君子，殿天子之邦。
帝謂文王：「無然畔援，無然歆羨，誕先登于岸。」密人不恭，敢距大邦，侵阮徂共。王赫斯怒，爰整其旅，以按徂旅，以篤于周祜，以對于天下。
豐年多黍多稂，亦有高廩，萬億及秭。為酒為醴，烝畀祖妣，以洽百禮，降福孔皆。

春秋
公及齊大夫盟于蔇。莊公九年。九月戊辰，諸侯盟于葵丘。僖公九年。
夏，楚人滅黃。僖公十有二年。楚人敗徐于婁林。僖公十有五年。秋，宋公、楚子、陳
translation_en:
…therefore feeling anxious concerning Heaven and the people. The Duke said: “Alas! My lord, you must understand the disposition of the people. None is incapable of making a beginning; it is the ending that matters. Reverently follow this, and go forth with care to govern.”
When ministers and people all comply, then excellence is truly manifest!

Book of Odes
Do not indulge excessively in ease; attend to the duties of your position. Delight in pleasure without excess; worthy men remain watchful.
Joyful is the noble man, who secures the realm of the Son of Heaven.
God on High said to King Wen: “Do not waver thus; do not covet thus. Be the first to ascend the bank.” The people of Mi were disrespectful: they dared resist the great state, invaded Ruan, and advanced to Gong. The king blazed with anger and marshalled his troops to check the advancing host, to strengthen Zhou’s blessings, and to answer the expectations of all under Heaven.
In a plentiful year there is much millet and much darnel [?], and there are lofty granaries, holding myriads upon myriads of measures. Make wine and sweet liquor, and present them to the ancestral fathers and mothers, completing the hundred rites; blessings descend in fullest measure.

Spring and Autumn Annals
The duke and a grand master of Qi made a covenant at Ji. Ninth year of Duke Zhuang. In the ninth month, on the wuchen day, the feudal lords made a covenant at Kuiqiu. Ninth year of Duke Xi.
In summer, the men of Chu destroyed Huang. Twelfth year of Duke Xi. The men of Chu defeated Xu at Loulin. Fifteenth year of Duke Xi. In autumn, the Duke of Song, the Viscount of Chu, and Chen…

title: 正德五年浙江鄉試錄
text:
侯蔡侯鄭伯許男曹伯會于盂執
宋公以伐宋〔俱僖公二十有一年〕公
以楚師伐齊取穀〔僖公二十有六年〕
冬楚人陳侯蔡侯鄭伯許男圍宋〔僖
公二十有七年〕夏四月己巳晉侯齊
師宋師秦師及楚人戰于城濮楚師
敗績〔僖公二十有八年〕
秦人伐晉〔文公三年〕
夏曹公孫會自鄭出奔宋〔昭公二十年〕
===
禮記
八州八伯五十六正百六十八帥三百三
十六長八伯各以其屬屬於天子之
老二人
人生而靜天之性也感於物而動性之欲
也物至知知然後好惡形焉
其在朝廷則道仁聖禮義之序
氣如白虹天也
第貳場
punctuated:
侯、蔡侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯會于盂，執宋公以伐宋。〔俱僖公二十有一年〕公以楚師伐齊，取穀。〔僖公二十有六年〕冬，楚人、陳侯、蔡侯、鄭伯、許男圍宋。〔僖公二十有七年〕夏，四月己巳，晉侯、齊師、宋師、秦師及楚人戰于城濮，楚師敗績。〔僖公二十有八年〕
秦人伐晉。〔文公三年〕
夏，曹公孫會自鄭出奔宋。〔昭公二十年〕

禮記
八州八伯，五十六正，百六十八帥，三百三十六長。八伯各以其屬屬於天子之老二人。
人生而靜，天之性也；感於物而動，性之欲也。物至知知，然後好惡形焉。
其在朝廷，則道仁聖禮義之序。
氣如白虹，天也。

第貳場
translation_en:
…the Marquis [of Chen], the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao met at Yu. They seized the Duke of Song and attacked Song. [Both entries belong to the twenty-first year of Duke Xi.] The duke led an army of Chu to attack Qi and captured Gu. [Twenty-sixth year of Duke Xi.] In winter, the men of Chu, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, and the Baron of Xu besieged Song. [Twenty-seventh year of Duke Xi.] In summer, on the jisi day of the fourth month, the Marquis of Jin and the armies of Qi, Song, and Qin fought the men of Chu at Chengpu. The army of Chu suffered a crushing defeat. [Twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi.]
The men of Qin attacked Jin. [Third year of Duke Wen.]
In summer, Gongsun Hui of Cao fled from Zheng to Song. [Twentieth year of Duke Zhao.]

Book of Rites
The eight provinces had eight regional chiefs, fifty-six overseers, one hundred and sixty-eight leaders, and three hundred and thirty-six heads. Each of the eight regional chiefs, together with his subordinates, was subject to the two senior ministers of the Son of Heaven.
Human beings are still at birth: this is their Heaven-given nature. When affected by external things, they become active: these are the desires of their nature. When things present themselves and awareness apprehends them, likes and dislikes then take shape.
At court, he speaks of the proper ordering of benevolence, sagacity, ritual propriety, and righteousness.
Vital energy like a white rainbow is of Heaven.

Second Session

title: 正德五年浙江鄉試錄
text:
論
大其心能體天下之物
詔誥表內科一道
擬漢憂郡國災異詔鴻嘉四年
擬唐加左僕射房玄齡太子少師誥貞觀
十三年
擬禮部率句容縣民謝
賜
御製嘉瓜贊表洪武五年
===
判語五條
封掌印信
轉解官物
服舍違式
關津留難
冒破物料
第叄場
策五道
問黃帝堯舜垂衣裳而天下治取諸乾坤
punctuated:
論：大其心，能體天下之物。

詔誥表內科一道：擬漢憂郡國災異詔，鴻嘉四年；擬唐加左僕射房玄齡太子少師誥，貞觀十三年；擬禮部率句容縣民謝賜御製嘉瓜贊表，洪武五年。

判語五條：封掌印信；轉解官物；服舍違式；關津留難；冒破物料。

第叄場

策五道。

問：黃帝、堯、舜垂衣裳而天下治，取諸乾坤，
translation_en:
Discourse
“Enlarge one's mind so that one can comprehend all things under Heaven.”

One composition from among the edict, proclamation, and memorial topics [科 doubtful]:
Draft an edict in the voice of a Han emperor expressing concern over disasters and anomalies in the commanderies and kingdoms: the fourth year of Hongjia.
Draft a Tang proclamation conferring on Fang Xuanling, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, the additional title of Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent: the thirteenth year of Zhenguan.
Draft a memorial in the voice of the Ministry of Rites, leading the people of Jurong County in thanking the emperor for bestowing his imperially composed “Eulogy on an Auspicious Melon”: the fifth year of Hongwu.

Five legal judgment topics:
Sealing and keeping custody of official seals.
Forwarding government goods.
Clothing and dwellings that violate prescribed regulations.
Obstruction and harassment at checkpoints and ferries.
Fraudulently claiming expenditure of materials.

Third Session

Five policy questions.

Question: “The Yellow Emperor, Yao, and Shun let their upper and lower garments hang down, and all under Heaven was well governed. They took this from the hexagrams Qian and Kun.” …

title: 正德五年浙江鄉試錄
text:
上棟下宇以待風雨取諸大壯夫衣服
宮室制度之末若可緩也然民志因之
而定夷夏因之而辨關繫治體為甚鉅
焉肇古逮今習尚不一求其反正有功
制作無議皆未有若我
太祖高皇帝者嘗叅古而論之如冠以竹皮則
冠制未定袍製金紫則服色未明我
朝尊卑冠服皆秩以官品俾不敢僭矧承左
衽之餘乎宅甲諸第則式有未定品無
===
公廨則制尚未立我
朝公私廬舍皆憲以定式俾不敢紊況易穹
廬之陋乎夫紹統治世厥功匪難纘緒
亂邦建制不易我
太祖當胡元汚夏之後獨能丕變其俗著為萬
世之典此所以有功天地度越古今非
後世帝王所可擬也昔孔子從周而美
郁郁之文諸士子躬逢
當代之盛不容默也其敬揚之毋忽
punctuated: 上棟下宇，以待風雨，取諸大壯。夫衣服、宮室，制度之末，若可緩也。然民志因之而定，夷夏因之而辨，關繫治體為甚鉅焉。肇古逮今，習尚不一，求其反正有功、制作無議，皆未有若我太祖高皇帝者。嘗叅古而論之，如冠以竹皮，則冠制未定；袍製金紫，則服色未明。我朝尊卑冠服，皆秩以官品，俾不敢僭，矧承左衽之餘乎！宅甲諸第，則式有未定；品無公廨，則制尚未立。我朝公私廬舍，皆憲以定式，俾不敢紊，況易穹廬之陋乎！夫紹統治世，厥功匪難；纘緒亂邦，建制不易。我太祖當胡元汚夏之後，獨能丕變其俗，著為萬世之典。此所以有功天地、度越古今，非後世帝王所可擬也。昔孔子從周，而美郁郁之文。諸士子躬逢當代之盛，不容默也。其敬揚之，毋忽！
translation_en:
…With ridgepoles above and eaves below to protect against wind and rain, they took their inspiration from the hexagram Dazhuang (Great Strength). Clothing and dwellings are minor aspects of institutional order and might seem capable of being deferred. Yet through them the people’s aspirations are settled and the distinction between the non-Chinese and the Chinese is made clear. Their bearing on the order of government is therefore immense. From earliest antiquity to the present, customs and preferences have varied. But among those who successfully restored proper order and established institutions beyond reproach, none has equaled our Emperor Taizu Gao.

Let us examine this in comparison with antiquity. When caps were made of bamboo bark, regulations for headgear were not yet settled; when robes were fashioned in gold and purple, the prescribed colors of dress were not yet clear. In our dynasty, the caps and garments of high and low alike are ordered according to official rank, so that none dares overstep his station. How much more significant is this achievement, coming after the legacy of fastening garments on the left! When a residence surpassed all other mansions, architectural standards were still unsettled; when official ranks lacked government offices [?], the system had yet to be established. In our dynasty, public and private dwellings alike conform to fixed standards, so that none dares introduce disorder. How much more significant is this achievement in replacing the crude domed tents!

To succeed to the imperial line in an age of order is no difficult achievement; to take up the succession in a realm beset by disorder and establish institutions is no easy matter. After the non-Chinese Yuan had defiled Chinese civilization, our Taizu alone was able profoundly to transform its customs and establish a lasting code for ten thousand generations. This is why his achievements benefited Heaven and Earth and surpassed past and present, beyond anything with which emperors of later ages could compare.

Confucius of old chose to follow Zhou and praised the richness of its cultural accomplishments. You examination candidates have personally encountered the flourishing age of the present dynasty and cannot remain silent. Reverently extol it, and do not be negligent!

title: 正德五年浙江鄉試錄
text:
問孔子嘗曰教民七年可以即戎子路亦
曰由也為之可使有勇蓋以道而言文
武相須以治而言文武並用不可偏廢
也稽之有周武教不外於文故武事不
出於學得人最盛克協文治可考而知
也至於漢則武帝有選成帝有募平帝
以下皆有詔所得之將或伸威外國或
坐困西羌或屢破匈奴或制平秦凉亦
可考而知也至於唐則開元有科大寳
===
有科槍射有法翹負有法其所得者往
往為國名臣禄山思明之難實有賴焉
至於宋則武學有官肄習有書内外有
舍考定去取高下有法其所得者往往
為時名將元昊智高之難實有賴焉亦
可考而知也若武舉所試為書者七為
韜者六為畧者三又皆可考而知也恭
惟我
孝宗敬皇帝雅意武舉
punctuated: 問：孔子嘗曰：「教民七年，可以即戎。」子路亦曰：「由也為之，可使有勇。」蓋以道而言，文武相須；以治而言，文武並用，不可偏廢也。稽之有周，武教不外於文，故武事不出於學，得人最盛，克協文治，可考而知也。至於漢，則武帝有選，成帝有募，平帝以下皆有詔。所得之將，或伸威外國，或坐困西羌，或屢破匈奴，或制平秦凉，亦可考而知也。至於唐，則開元有科，大寳有科，槍射有法，翹負有法。其所得者，往往為國名臣，禄山、思明之難，實有賴焉。至於宋，則武學有官，肄習有書，内外有舍，考定去取高下有法。其所得者，往往為時名將，元昊、智高之難，實有賴焉，亦可考而知也。若武舉所試，為書者七，為韜者六，為畧者三，又皆可考而知也。恭惟我孝宗敬皇帝雅意武舉
translation_en:
Question: Confucius once said, “After teaching the common people for seven years, one may lead them into warfare.” Zilu also said, “If I, You, were to administer it, I could make its people courageous.” In terms of the Way, civil and military accomplishments depend upon one another; in terms of government, both must be employed, and neither may be neglected. Examining the Zhou, we find that military instruction was not separate from civil learning, and military training therefore remained within the schools. Its success in obtaining capable men was unsurpassed, and they effectively supported civil government: this can be established through investigation. Under the Han, Emperor Wu selected men, Emperor Cheng recruited them, and Emperor Ping and his successors all issued edicts. Among the generals thus obtained, some extended their might into foreign countries; some found themselves beset by the Western Qiang; some repeatedly defeated the Xiongnu; and some subdued and pacified Qin and Liang. This, too, can be established through investigation.

Under the Tang, there were examination categories in the Kaiyuan era and in the Dabao era [?], with prescribed methods for spear work and archery, and for qiaofu [?]. Those thus obtained often became renowned ministers of the state, and the state indeed relied upon them during the rebellions of Lushan and Siming. Under the Song, military schools had appointed officials, texts for study, inner and outer divisions, and rules governing assessment, acceptance or rejection, and ranking. Those thus obtained often became renowned generals of their time, and the state indeed relied upon them during the rebellions of Yuanhao and Zhigao. This, too, can be established through investigation.

As for the texts tested in the military examinations, there were seven books, six Teachings, and three Strategies—all likewise ascertainable through investigation. We reverently reflect that our Emperor Xiaozong Jing had a deep interest in the military examinations …

title: 正德五年浙江鄉試錄
text:
今上繼述遂舉行之騎射程才論策課學得文
武士以脩我戎諸生所目擊也讀其書
論其世商其法數其人之姓名而參訂
其是非得失皆學者能事蓋深有望於
諸生也幸詳以告
問民受天地之中以生所謂命也天之生
人宜無彼此厚薄之私而人之生每有
貧賤富貴之等壽夭禍福之異而憂樂
於是乎生焉通塞於是乎判焉或者曰
===
富與貴在我而已以智則得也何命之
為若然則以俟命為愚矣而古之人乃
不改於陋巷之樂不病夫衣冠之敝梁
父之吟恬然於草廬之中精舍之心不
動於除書之到涪州之行講道自如也
南海之謫吟詩自若也甚而有將死而
泰然不憂者有將就刑而神色不動者
其心何主哉或者曰求之有不得而不
求有得之者皆命也人事何為若然則
punctuated:
今上繼述，遂舉行之。騎射程才，論策課學，得文武士，以脩我戎，諸生所目擊也。讀其書，論其世，商其法，數其人之姓名，而參訂其是非得失，皆學者能事。蓋深有望於諸生也，幸詳以告。
問：民受天地之中以生，所謂命也。天之生人，宜無彼此厚薄之私，而人之生，每有貧賤富貴之等，壽夭禍福之異，而憂樂於是乎生焉，通塞於是乎判焉。或者曰：「富與貴，在我而已，以智則得也，何命之為？」若然，則以俟命為愚矣。而古之人乃不改於陋巷之樂，不病夫衣冠之敝；梁父之吟，恬然於草廬之中；精舍之心，不動於除書之到；涪州之行，講道自如也；南海之謫，吟詩自若也。甚而有將死而泰然不憂者，有將就刑而神色不動者，其心何主哉？或者曰：「求之有不得，而不求有得之者，皆命也，人事何為？」若然則
translation_en:
…The present emperor carried forward his predecessor’s intentions and accordingly instituted it. Riding and archery assess ability; discourses and policy essays test learning. Thus men accomplished in letters and arms are recruited to put our military affairs in order, as you candidates have witnessed yourselves. To read their books, consider their times, deliberate on their methods, enumerate these men by name, and compare and assess their rights and wrongs, successes and failures—all these lie within a scholar’s competence. We place great hopes in you candidates; please give a detailed account.
Question: People are born receiving the balanced essence of Heaven and Earth: this is what is called destiny. In giving birth to human beings, Heaven ought to show no partiality, favoring some and slighting others. Yet human lives invariably differ in poverty and low status, wealth and high rank, longevity and early death, misfortune and good fortune. From these arise sorrow and joy; through these, fulfillment and frustration are distinguished. Some say: “Wealth and high rank depend on me alone. With cleverness I can obtain them. What has destiny to do with it?” If so, awaiting destiny would be foolish. Yet men of antiquity retained their joy while living in humble lanes and were untroubled by worn-out robes and caps. One chanted the Song of Liangfu, content within his thatched cottage; another’s heart, settled in his scholarly retreat, remained unmoved when a letter of appointment arrived. One journeyed to Fuzhou and continued expounding the Way as usual; another, banished to Nanhai, continued composing poetry with equanimity. There were even those who faced imminent death serenely, without anxiety, and those whose expressions remained unchanged as they approached execution. What governed their hearts? Some say: “That one may seek something without obtaining it, while another obtains it without seeking, is all destiny. What use is human effort?” If so, then…

title: 正德五年浙江鄉試錄
text:
以徼幸為非矣而昔之人乃輒為窮途
之哭動興附郭之歎長安下淚頓移於
得意之春風帝鄉空囊却誤於樓上之
攘奪逆旅奇遇而竟以流落內署久對
而終於見棄甚而有欲打墨本而雷轟
其碑者有欲得館職而脩書至死者其
計何如哉夫命一也有聖人之所罕言
者有君子之所當知者於聖人之所罕
言者固未易以強言而君子之所當知
===
者自聖人以至於凡人皆不可以不知
故孔子進以禮退以義得之不得曰有
命此聖人之安命也諸士子學聖人者
也試為我言之將以觀子之進退之節
焉
問士莫先於立身而廉耻立身之大節也
人而無耻遂至於有函谷之雞鳴村莊
之犬吠入錢五百萬胡椒八百斛方且
侈然自得而畧無沮喪之心者是又惡
punctuated:
以徼幸為非矣。而昔之人乃輒為窮途之哭，動興附郭之歎；長安下淚，頓移於得意之春風；帝鄉空囊，却誤於樓上之攘奪；逆旅奇遇，而竟以流落；內署久對，而終於見棄。甚而有欲打墨本而雷轟其碑者，有欲得館職而脩書至死者，其計何如哉？夫命一也，有聖人之所罕言者，有君子之所當知者。於聖人之所罕言者，固未易以強言；而君子之所當知者，自聖人以至於凡人，皆不可以不知。故孔子進以禮，退以義，得之不得，曰有命。此聖人之安命也。諸士子學聖人者也，試為我言之，將以觀子之進退之節焉。

問：士莫先於立身，而廉耻，立身之大節也。人而無耻，遂至於有函谷之雞鳴、村莊之犬吠、入錢五百萬、胡椒八百斛，方且侈然自得，而畧無沮喪之心者，是又惡
translation_en:
…one would regard seeking good fortune through chance as wrong. Yet men of former times would weep upon reaching an impassable road, or readily sigh over the lack of fields outside the city walls. Tears shed in Chang’an abruptly gave way to the spring breeze of success; an empty purse in the imperial capital led instead, through a mishap, to plunder in an upper chamber [?]. An extraordinary encounter at an inn nevertheless ended in a life of wandering; prolonged audiences in the inner offices ended in rejection. There were even men who wished to take an ink rubbing, only for thunder to shatter the stele, and men who sought an appointment in a literary institute and labored at compiling books until they died. What are we to make of their calculations?

Destiny is one, yet it has aspects of which the sage seldom spoke and aspects that the gentleman ought to understand. As for those of which the sage seldom spoke, it is certainly difficult to insist on speaking of them. But those that the gentleman ought to understand must be understood by everyone, from sages down to ordinary people. Thus Confucius advanced in accordance with ritual propriety and withdrew in accordance with righteousness; whether he obtained what he sought or not, he said that destiny governed it. This was the sage’s acceptance of destiny. You candidates are men who learn from the sage. Explain this for me, so that I may assess the principles governing your advancement and withdrawal.

Question: For a scholar, nothing takes precedence over establishing his moral character, and integrity and a sense of shame are its cardinal principles. When people lack shame, they may go so far as to imitate a cock’s crow at Hangu Pass or a dog’s bark in a village, pay in five million in cash, or possess eight hundred hu of pepper. Yet they remain extravagantly pleased with themselves, without the slightest feeling of dismay. How could such people…

title: 正德五年浙江鄉試錄
text:
足與言人道哉間有知廉恥爲重而其
跡每每有相齟齬者金珠貝玉舉世所
慕也而生平手不之執其視兼金之受
者何懸絕耶水濱井內非有所主也而
飲馬必投之錢其視一介不與者何徑
庭耶非其耕與力則不食守之固矣然
則傳食於諸侯者不曰泰乎居將與相
而布被操之約矣然則累茵而坐者不
曰侈乎居室一也有爲其子孫而不營
===
者有爲其兄而不居者有爲其兄而不
毁者其得失何在田產一也有欲全其
身而多請者有欲完其節而不買者有
欲傳其家而不問者其是非何居之數
者皆辭受居處之大而日用之所不能
無也茲欲擇其中而用之諸士子講貫
於平昔熟矣其明以告我毋隱
問水旱之災自古有之然災之未至有消
弭之道災之旣罹有拯救之術受民社
punctuated:
足與言人道哉？間有知廉恥爲重，而其跡每每有相齟齬者。金珠貝玉，舉世所慕也，而生平手不之執，其視兼金之受者，何懸絕耶？水濱井內，非有所主也，而飲馬必投之錢，其視一介不與者，何徑庭耶？非其耕與力則不食，守之固矣；然則傳食於諸侯者，不曰泰乎？居將與相而布被，操之約矣；然則累茵而坐者，不曰侈乎？居室一也，有爲其子孫而不營者，有爲其兄而不居者，有爲其兄而不毁者，其得失何在？田產一也，有欲全其身而多請者，有欲完其節而不買者，有欲傳其家而不問者，其是非何居？之數者，皆辭受居處之大，而日用之所不能無也。茲欲擇其中而用之，諸士子講貫於平昔熟矣，其明以告我，毋隱。
問：水旱之災，自古有之。然災之未至，有消弭之道；災之旣罹，有拯救之術。受民社
translation_en:
…how could such people be fit to discuss the proper human way? Yet some recognize the importance of integrity and a sense of shame, while their conduct often seems mutually contradictory. Gold, pearls, cowries, and jade are coveted by the whole world, yet one man never touched them throughout his life. How very different he was from one who accepted gold of double value! The water beside a river or within a well has no particular owner, yet another man invariably cast in money when watering his horse. How far his conduct diverged from that of one who would not give away even the smallest thing!
One would eat nothing unless it came from his own tilling and labor: firm indeed was his adherence to principle. Yet would this not make one who received sustenance successively from the feudal lords excessively indulgent? Another used a cloth quilt even while holding office as general or chief minister: frugal indeed was his practice. Yet would this not make one who sat upon piled cushions extravagant?
Consider the same matter of dwellings: one declined to build a house for the sake of his descendants; another declined to occupy one for his elder brother’s sake; and another declined to demolish one for his elder brother’s sake. Where did they act rightly or wrongly? Consider likewise landed property: one requested much of it to preserve his life; another declined to purchase it to preserve his integrity; and another, wishing to perpetuate his family, made no inquiries about it. Wherein lay the right and wrong of these actions?
These several cases [?] all concern major questions of declining and accepting, residence and conduct, which inevitably arise in daily life. I now wish to select and apply the proper mean among them. You examination candidates have long discussed and thoroughly studied these matters. Explain them clearly to me, withholding nothing.
Question: Floods and droughts have occurred since antiquity. Before a calamity arrives, however, there are ways to avert it; once it has struck, there are methods of relief. Those entrusted with the people and the altars of the soil…

title: 正德五年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之寄者所宜討論也宋儒有言脩德行
政以應天也而比歲之旱今茲之潦奸
和天地其咎安在可謂善言災矣方今
朝廷厲精更化內外庶政秉公協恭所以應
天者亦至矣而
京師不雨四方多災以兩浙言之往歲則旱
魃為虐今春則霖潦為殃所以干天地
之和者誰任其咎將歸之天數歟抑責
之人事歟宋大儒嘗行荒政於浙東興
===
水利於黃巖皆所以防災救災也其詳
可得聞歟抑可以舉而行之歟主司策
士不欲以詖辭隱義相困而獨以是為
問蓋今浙事無有大於此者亦無有急
於此者固諸士子所身履有司所心憂
者當有確論願極言之
punctuated: 之寄者所宜討論也。宋儒有言：「脩德行政以應天也，而比歲之旱、今茲之潦，奸和天地，其咎安在？」可謂善言災矣。方今朝廷厲精更化，內外庶政，秉公協恭，所以應天者亦至矣。而京師不雨，四方多災。以兩浙言之，往歲則旱魃為虐，今春則霖潦為殃，所以干天地之和者，誰任其咎？將歸之天數歟？抑責之人事歟？宋大儒嘗行荒政於浙東，興水利於黃巖，皆所以防災救災也。其詳可得聞歟？抑可以舉而行之歟？主司策士，不欲以詖辭隱義相困，而獨以是為問。蓋今浙事無有大於此者，亦無有急於此者，固諸士子所身履、有司所心憂者。當有確論，願極言之。
translation_en:
…are matters that those entrusted with responsibility for the people and the altars of the soil ought to examine. A Confucian scholar of the Song said: “Cultivate virtue and conduct government in response to Heaven. Yet droughts in recent years and floods this year have disrupted the harmony of Heaven and Earth [?]: where does the blame lie?” This may be called an insightful statement about disasters.

At present, the court is applying itself diligently to reform; in all affairs of government, officials within and outside the capital uphold impartiality and cooperate respectfully. Their efforts to respond to Heaven have indeed been thorough. Yet no rain falls in the capital, and disasters abound throughout the realm. Speaking of the Two Zhe regions, in past years the drought demon wrought havoc; this spring, prolonged rains and flooding have brought calamity. Who bears the blame for what has disturbed the harmony of Heaven and Earth? Shall we attribute it to Heaven’s allotted fate, or hold human affairs responsible?

A great Confucian scholar of the Song once implemented famine relief measures in Zhedong and developed waterworks in Huangyan, all intended to prevent disasters and relieve their effects. May we hear the details? And could these measures be put into practice?

In examining candidates through policy questions, the presiding examiners do not wish to perplex you with misleading language and obscure meanings, but ask specifically about this matter. For among the affairs of Zhejiang today, none is greater or more urgent. This is indeed something you candidates have experienced personally and that weighs upon the responsible officials’ minds. You should have well-founded judgments; we hope you will express them fully.

title: 正德五年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
敬事而信節用而愛人使民以時
戴𨺲
同考試官訓導洪批揭書出題初無所主作者
多以務本相因立論故詞愈繁而意愈晦此篇文
從理順體認詳明執此可以占子之從政矣
同考試官學正佘批此篇於治國之要立論平
易措辭雅實殆亦知要者歟
===
考試官學正李批拍仲文字間似此甚少
考試官學正張批以文敘事此作近之
聖人於治國之要而必歷舉其目焉蓋治國之
道固為多端而其要則有五也苟能舉而行之
於治乎何有宜聖人歷舉之以為君人者告也
吾想其意若曰人君治千乘之國不患乎政之
不成而患乎要之未得其要維何亦曰敬信節
愛時使五者而已何則敬為萬事之權輿非敬
則事不集矣必主一之心恒矜持於宰制之時
punctuated:
第壹塲
四書
敬事而信，節用而愛人，使民以時。
戴𨺲
同考試官訓導洪批：揭書出題，初無所主，作者多以務本相因立論，故詞愈繁而意愈晦。此篇文從理順，體認詳明，執此可以占子之從政矣。
同考試官學正佘批：此篇於治國之要，立論平易，措辭雅實，殆亦知要者歟？
考試官學正李批：拍仲文字間，似此甚少。
考試官學正張批：以文敘事，此作近之。
聖人於治國之要，而必歷舉其目焉。蓋治國之道固為多端，而其要則有五也。苟能舉而行之，於治乎何有？宜聖人歷舉之，以為君人者告也。吾想其意若曰：人君治千乘之國，不患乎政之不成，而患乎要之未得。其要維何？亦曰敬、信、節、愛、時使五者而已。何則？敬為萬事之權輿，非敬則事不集矣。必主一之心恒矜持於宰制之時
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“Be reverent in attending to affairs and trustworthy; be frugal in expenditure and cherish the people; employ the people at the proper seasons.”
Dai [given name 𨺲, reading uncertain].
Comment by Associate Examiner Hong, Assistant Instructor: When the book was opened and the topic selected, no particular interpretation was intended. Many writers based their arguments on the successive connections among these efforts to attend to fundamentals; hence, the more elaborate their wording, the more obscure their meaning became. In this essay, the prose flows naturally and the reasoning proceeds smoothly; its understanding is thorough and clear. From this, one can judge how you will conduct yourself in government.
Comment by Associate Examiner She, Instructor: On the essentials of governing a state, this essay presents an accessible argument in language both elegant and substantive. Might its author also be someone who understands the essentials?
Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: Among the writings of “paizhong” [?], very few are like this.
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: This work comes close to using literary expression to set forth affairs.
In discussing the essentials of governing a state, the Sage necessarily enumerated each item. For although the ways of governing a state are indeed manifold, their essentials number five. If one can put them all into practice, what difficulty is there in governing? It was fitting that the Sage should enumerate them as instruction for those who rule over others. I imagine his meaning to have been as follows: When a ruler governs a state of a thousand chariots, he should worry not that his administration will fail, but that he has not grasped its essentials. What are those essentials? They are simply these five: reverence, trustworthiness, frugality, love, and employing the people at the proper seasons. Why is this so? Reverence is the starting point of all affairs; without it, affairs cannot be accomplished. One must constantly maintain a mind intent on a single purpose while directing and regulating affairs …

title: 正德五年浙江鄉試錄
text:
不以事之大小而有異無適之念每恪存於顯
設之際不以事之難易而有殊固不敢忽於其
始亦不敢怠於其終焉信為人君之大寶不信
則民弗從矣故有所敷宣也推以至誠務恊群
黎之心志有所期會也發自中孚毋眩百姓之
聽聞不持疑於可否不紛更於旦夕焉敬事也
信也非治國之要乎國以財為用財不節用何
由而舒邪必量入為出而惜乎有限之財制節
謹度不侈於無經之費務使軍國之需不竭於
===
府庫之積而於用斯為節矣國以人為本人不
愛本安得而固邪必體大造之仁而保民如子
擴同胞之念而視民如傷務俾子惠之政溥及
於閭閻之間而於人斯為愛矣節用也愛人也
非治國之要乎至若農時乃民所恃以為生而
不可奪者如國有當作之事也必俟其力農之
餘而後使之趨有當興之工也必乘其服穡之
暇而後使之赴寧緩於興作而不緩於民事是
使民以時又非治國之要乎吁人君果能行此
punctuated: 不以事之大小而有異，無適之念每恪存於顯設之際，不以事之難易而有殊，固不敢忽於其始，亦不敢怠於其終焉。信為人君之大寶，不信則民弗從矣。故有所敷宣也，推以至誠，務恊群黎之心志；有所期會也，發自中孚，毋眩百姓之聽聞。不持疑於可否，不紛更於旦夕焉。敬事也，信也，非治國之要乎？國以財為用，財不節，用何由而舒邪？必量入為出，而惜乎有限之財；制節謹度，不侈於無經之費，務使軍國之需不竭於府庫之積，而於用斯為節矣。國以人為本，人不愛，本安得而固邪？必體大造之仁，而保民如子；擴同胞之念，而視民如傷，務俾子惠之政溥及於閭閻之間，而於人斯為愛矣。節用也，愛人也，非治國之要乎？至若農時，乃民所恃以為生而不可奪者。如國有當作之事也，必俟其力農之餘，而後使之趨；有當興之工也，必乘其服穡之暇，而後使之赴。寧緩於興作，而不緩於民事，是使民以時，又非治國之要乎？吁！人君果能行此
translation_en:
…without making any distinction according to whether affairs are great or small. A mind that does not stray must always be scrupulously maintained when putting measures into effect [?], without making any distinction according to whether affairs are difficult or easy. One must dare neither to be careless at their beginning nor to grow lax at their end. Trustworthiness is a ruler’s great treasure; without it, the people will not follow him. Thus, whenever he makes a proclamation, he must extend the utmost sincerity, striving to bring the hearts and intentions of the common people into accord. Whenever he sets an appointed time for assembly, he must act from inward sincerity, without confusing the people about what they hear. He must not waver over what is acceptable or change his decisions repeatedly from morning to evening. Are reverence in attending to affairs and trustworthiness not essentials of governing a state?

A state relies on wealth for its expenditures. If wealth is not husbanded, how can its expenditure be comfortably sustained? The ruler must determine expenditure according to revenue and cherish his finite resources. He must establish restraints and observe limits carefully, avoiding extravagance in unregulated expenses, and ensure that military and governmental needs do not exhaust the reserves in the treasuries. This is economy in expenditure. A state takes its people as its foundation. If the people are not cherished, how can that foundation be secure? The ruler must embody the benevolence of the great creative power of Heaven and Earth and protect the people as his children. He must extend the sense that all are his siblings and regard the people as though they were injured. He must ensure that government which cherishes them as children reaches throughout the residential lanes. This is love for the people. Are economy in expenditure and love for the people not essentials of governing a state?

As for the farming seasons, the people depend on them for their livelihood and must not be deprived of them. If the state has tasks that must be undertaken, the ruler must wait until the people have time left over from their agricultural labors before making them hasten to those tasks. If there are works that must be initiated, he must take advantage of their respite from cultivating crops before making them go to the works. Better to delay public works than to delay the people’s agricultural affairs. This is employing the people at the proper times: is it not also an essential of governing a state? Ah! If a ruler can truly put these into practice…

title: 正德五年浙江鄉試錄
text:
五者則所操者約而所及者博治國之要孰有
過於此哉雖然五者之中又當以敬爲本蓋持
之以敬則中有主而自治嚴信與節愛時使凡
見諸施爲者自然不苟而至治可馴致矣聖人
言雖至近上下皆通此三言者若推其極堯舜
之治亦不過此惜乎世以智謀功利爲尚而不
足以語此治不古若有由然夫
中立而不倚強哉矯
葉忠
===
同考試官教諭張 批中立不倚難於立言典實
若此篇學能窮理者錄之
同考試官教諭張 批昌於辭而不謬於理作中
庸義能若此殆嘗用心於理學者歟
同考試官學正賈 批理學文字下筆便難此篇
敷析明潔非卓有定見者不能錄之宜矣
考試官學正李 批簡净無疵
考試官學正張 批說理通徹
論君子有特立之操見君子有自勝之強蓋所
punctuated:
五者，則所操者約，而所及者博，治國之要孰有過於此哉？雖然，五者之中，又當以敬爲本。蓋持之以敬，則中有主而自治嚴，信與節、愛、時使，凡見諸施爲者，自然不苟，而至治可馴致矣。聖人言雖至近，上下皆通。此三言者，若推其極，堯舜之治亦不過此。惜乎世以智謀功利爲尚，而不足以語此！治不古若，有由然夫！

中立而不倚，強哉矯！
葉忠

同考試官教諭張，批：「中立不倚，難於立言。典實若此篇，學能窮理者，錄之。」
同考試官教諭張，批：「昌於辭而不謬於理，作中庸義能若此，殆嘗用心於理學者歟？」
同考試官學正賈，批：「理學文字，下筆便難。此篇敷析明潔，非卓有定見者不能，錄之宜矣。」
考試官學正李，批：「簡净無疵。」
考試官學正張，批：「說理通徹。」

論君子有特立之操，見君子有自勝之強。蓋所
translation_en:
…these five practices, then what the ruler holds to is simple, while its effects are far-reaching. What essentials of governing a state could surpass these? Nevertheless, among these five, reverent attentiveness must be the foundation. For if one maintains them with reverent attentiveness, one has a master within and governs oneself strictly. Trustworthiness, economy, care for others, and employing the people at the proper seasons—all that finds expression in action—will naturally be free of carelessness, and perfect government can gradually be attained. Although the sage’s words are very accessible, they apply alike to those above and below. If these three statements are carried to their fullest extent, even the government of Yao and Shun goes no further. Alas, the world prizes clever schemes, achievement, and profit, and is unfit to discuss this! There is indeed a reason why government does not equal that of antiquity!

“He stands in the center without leaning to either side: how firm his strength!”
Ye Zhong 葉忠

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “It is difficult to formulate an argument on standing in the center without leaning to either side. An essay as well grounded and substantial as this is the work of someone whose learning enables him to investigate principle fully. Select it.”

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “Fluent in expression without departing from principle: someone who can compose an exposition on the Doctrine of the Mean like this has surely devoted thought to the learning of principle.”

Associate Examiner Jia, School Instructor, comments: “Writing on the learning of principle is difficult from the moment one takes up the brush. This essay’s exposition and analysis are clear and lucid; only someone with outstanding and firmly established understanding could achieve this. It certainly deserves selection.”

Examiner Li, School Instructor, comments: “Concise, clean, and without blemish.”

Examiner Zhang, School Instructor, comments: “Its explanation of principle is thorough and penetrating.”

In discussing the gentleman’s integrity in standing independently, we see his strength in mastering himself. For what…

title: 正德五年浙江鄉試錄
text:
貴乎強者以其有特立之操也君子自立於中
而無所倚焉非自勝之強能若是乎是宜聖人
深賛之也昔夫子因子路問強告以所當強者
及此謂夫道之所貴者中是中也原於帝降為
天理之精微著於民彝為人心之極致自夫衆
人不察能立於中者鮮矣君子則存養以立其
體省察以達其用視至正之域為依歸卓然而
自樹以至當之理為標的挺然而自持窮通得
喪惟中是居固無太過亦無不及也夷險順逆
===
惟中是履高不過亢卑不過貶也夫中立無依
鮮有不倚者矣君子則心不移於外誘志不惑
於他岐其立於中也不假維持自不至於偃仆
無俟依附自不至於傾側窮通得喪勢雖變於
前而中立之守不與之俱變貫始終而一致也
夷險順逆境雖易於前而中立之節不與之俱
易歷久暫而一轍也夫自立非難中立為難中
立固難不倚尤難也君子中立而不倚是其擇
之已精守之已固吾知理足以勝私氣足以配
punctuated: 貴乎強者，以其有特立之操也。君子自立於中，而無所倚焉，非自勝之強能若是乎？是宜聖人深賛之也。昔夫子因子路問強，告以所當強者，及此謂夫道之所貴者中。是中也，原於帝降，為天理之精微；著於民彝，為人心之極致。自夫衆人不察，能立於中者鮮矣。君子則存養以立其體，省察以達其用，視至正之域為依歸，卓然而自樹；以至當之理為標的，挺然而自持。窮通得喪，惟中是居，固無太過，亦無不及也；夷險順逆，惟中是履，高不過亢，卑不過貶也。夫中立無依，鮮有不倚者矣。君子則心不移於外誘，志不惑於他岐。其立於中也，不假維持，自不至於偃仆；無俟依附，自不至於傾側。窮通得喪，勢雖變於前，而中立之守不與之俱變，貫始終而一致也；夷險順逆，境雖易於前，而中立之節不與之俱易，歷久暫而一轍也。夫自立非難，中立為難；中立固難，不倚尤難也。君子中立而不倚，是其擇之已精，守之已固。吾知理足以勝私，氣足以配
translation_en:
…what makes strength worthy of esteem is the integrity that enables one to stand independently. The gentleman establishes himself in the Mean and leans on nothing. Could he achieve this without the strength to overcome himself? It is fitting, then, that the sage should praise him deeply. In former times, when Zilu asked about strength, the Master instructed him concerning the strength he ought to cultivate, reaching this point: what is valued in the Way is the Mean. This Mean originates in what the Lord on High bestows and constitutes the subtle essence of Heaven’s principle; it manifests itself in the enduring norms of human relationships and constitutes the highest attainment of the human heart. Since ordinary people fail to discern it, few can take their stand in the Mean. The gentleman, however, preserves and nourishes his moral nature to establish its substance, and examines himself to realize its functioning. He takes the realm of utmost rectitude as his refuge and stands resolutely on his own; he takes the principle of utmost appropriateness as his standard and steadfastly maintains himself. In adversity or success, gain or loss, he abides only in the Mean, neither going too far nor falling short. Through ease or danger, favorable or adverse circumstances, he treads only the Mean: when high, he does not lapse into arrogance; when low, he does not sink into self-abasement.

To stand in the Mean without support—few indeed can do so without leaning on something. But the gentleman’s heart is not swayed by external temptations, nor is his resolve confused by divergent paths. In standing in the Mean, he needs no support to keep him from falling; he awaits no external attachment to keep him from tilting to either side. In adversity or success, gain or loss, circumstances may change before him, but his commitment to standing in the Mean does not change with them: it remains consistent from beginning to end. Through ease or danger, favorable or adverse circumstances, his situation may alter before him, but his integrity in standing in the Mean does not alter with it: whether the duration is long or short, he follows the same course. To stand independently is not difficult; to stand in the Mean is difficult. Standing in the Mean is indeed difficult, but not leaning on anything is harder still. The gentleman stands in the Mean without leaning: his discernment in choosing it is already precise, and his adherence to it already firm. I know that his grasp of principle suffices to overcome selfishness, and his vital energy suffices to accord with…

title: 正德五年浙江鄉試錄
text:
道超乎流俗既不失於南方之不及伸於萬物
亦不失於北方之大過其爲強也雖壁立萬仞
不足以喻之矣豈不矯矯乎可尚哉雖氣奪三
軍不足以儗之矣又不矯矯乎可嘉哉君子之
強如此此所以爲德義之勇而子路所當致力
者歟抑此特論其勇達道之一耳究其進爲之
序而要其歸宿之區必知仁兼盡始無缺焉蓋
知以知此仁以體此勇以強此知不如舜仁不
如回勇不如夫子之告子路則求愈切而道愈
===
離不以爲難而不敢爲則以爲易而不足爲矣
然則將何所從事乎亦惟先立乎誠以入於德
孔子登東山而小魯登太山而小天下
柴經
同考試官訓導方 批 題意甚明作者體認不真
謂孔子親登是山鑿亦甚矣此篇見理明白造語整
嚴特用錄出以釋羣疑
考試官學正李 批 孟子善言聖道之大子能敷
析孟子之言程度之文如此篇者可多見乎即此可覘
punctuated:
道，超乎流俗，既不失於南方之不及；伸於萬物，亦不失於北方之大過。其爲強也，雖壁立萬仞，不足以喻之矣，豈不矯矯乎可尚哉？雖氣奪三軍，不足以儗之矣，又不矯矯乎可嘉哉？君子之強如此，此所以爲德義之勇，而子路所當致力者歟！抑此特論其勇，達道之一耳。究其進爲之序，而要其歸宿之區，必知仁兼盡，始無缺焉。蓋知以知此，仁以體此，勇以強此。知不如舜，仁不如回，勇不如夫子之告子路，則求愈切而道愈離。不以爲難而不敢爲，則以爲易而不足爲矣。然則將何所從事乎？亦惟先立乎誠，以入於德。
孔子登東山而小魯，登太山而小天下。
柴經
同考試官訓導方批：題意甚明，作者體認不真，謂孔子親登是山，鑿亦甚矣。此篇見理明白，造語整嚴，特用錄出，以釋羣疑。
考試官學正李批：孟子善言聖道之大，子能敷析孟子之言。程度之文如此篇者，可多見乎？即此可覘
translation_en:
…the Way. Rising above prevailing customs, he avoids the deficiency of the strength of the south; standing tall amid all things, he likewise avoids the excess of the strength of the north. Such is his strength that even a sheer cliff ten thousand ren high cannot adequately illustrate it. Is it not outstanding and worthy of esteem? Even a spirit that overawes the Three Armies cannot compare with it. Is it not likewise outstanding and worthy of praise? Such is the gentleman’s strength. This is why it constitutes courage grounded in virtue and righteousness, and why Zilu ought to devote himself to it!
Yet this discusses only his courage, just one of the universally applicable virtues. To investigate the sequence of his advancement and establish its ultimate destination, wisdom and benevolence must also be fully realized; only then will nothing be lacking. Wisdom serves to understand this, benevolence to embody it, and courage to strengthen it. If one’s wisdom falls short of Shun’s, one’s benevolence falls short of Hui’s, and one’s courage falls short of what the Master described to Zilu, then the more urgently one seeks, the further one departs from the Way. One either regards it as difficult and dares not undertake it, or regards it as easy and unworthy of undertaking [?]. What, then, should one set about doing? One must first establish oneself in sincerity, thereby entering into virtue.
“When Confucius ascended the Eastern Mountain, he regarded Lu as small; when he ascended Mount Tai, he regarded all under Heaven as small.”
Chai Jing
Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, an Assistant Instructor: “The meaning of the topic is perfectly clear, but writers fail to grasp it truly. To say that Confucius personally climbed these mountains is exceedingly forced. This essay understands the principle clearly, and its wording is orderly and rigorous. It has been specially selected for inclusion to resolve the various doubts.”
Comment by Examiner Li, an Instructor: “Mencius excels at describing the greatness of the sage’s Way, and you are able to expound and analyze Mencius’s words. Can essays that meet the prescribed standard as this one does be encountered often? From this alone one can discern…”

title: 正德五年浙江鄉試錄
text:
所負矣
考試官學正張批豐約中度文字最佳者
大賢狀聖道之大隨其所處之高異其所視之
小蓋所處者高則其視下自不容於不小也聖
人隨所處而小其所視焉其道之大不於是而
可見哉孟子形容以示人厥有旨矣想其意若
謂道莫大於聖人聖莫盛於孔子參乎天地憲
萬世而莫倫冠乎古今高百王而莫並孔子其
登東山乎蓋魯國之鉅山亦多矣惟夫東山拔
===
峙境內爲一方之具瞻雄據域中作是邦之偉
觀東山旣登則一時望國傾目以無餘百里提
封注望而殆盡龜蒙左右一指而祇見其卑鳧
繹後先一盻而第覺其隘是豈魯小乎東山之
高迥乎魯國自東山視之不爲不小矣孔子之
道大無與儔一登東山而小魯耳孰能比擬之
哉孔子其登太山乎蓋天下之大山不少矣惟
夫太山尊踰華岱屹乎五嶽之攸宗高壓鴻龐
巍乎九州之鉅鎮太山旣登則宇宙寥廓眇然
punctuated:
所負矣。
考試官學正張批：豐約中度，文字最佳者。
大賢狀聖道之大，隨其所處之高，異其所視之小。蓋所處者高，則其視下自不容於不小也。聖人隨所處而小其所視焉，其道之大不於是而可見哉？孟子形容以示人，厥有旨矣。想其意若謂：道莫大於聖人，聖莫盛於孔子。參乎天地，憲萬世而莫倫；冠乎古今，高百王而莫並。孔子其登東山乎？蓋魯國之鉅山亦多矣，惟夫東山拔峙境內，爲一方之具瞻；雄據域中，作是邦之偉觀。東山旣登，則一時望國，傾目以無餘；百里提封，注望而殆盡。龜蒙左右，一指而祇見其卑；鳧繹後先，一盻而第覺其隘。是豈魯小乎？東山之高迥乎魯國，自東山視之，不爲不小矣。孔子之道大無與儔，一登東山而小魯耳，孰能比擬之哉？孔子其登太山乎？蓋天下之大山不少矣，惟夫太山尊踰華岱，屹乎五嶽之攸宗；高壓鴻龐，巍乎九州之鉅鎮。太山旣登，則宇宙寥廓，眇然
translation_en:
…the capacities he possesses.
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “Fullness and brevity are properly balanced; this is writing of the highest quality.”
The great worthy describes the greatness of the sage’s Way: as the height of his position changes, so does the smallness of what he sees. For when one occupies a high position, what one looks down upon cannot but appear small. The sage regards what he sees as small in accordance with the position he occupies. Is not the greatness of his Way visible in this? Mencius had a particular purpose in portraying this for others. We may imagine his meaning to be as follows: no Way is greater than that of the sages, and no sage more consummate than Confucius. He stands alongside Heaven and Earth, a model for ten thousand generations without equal; he surpasses all of antiquity and the present, loftier than a hundred kings, with none to match him.
Did Confucius then ascend Mount Dong? There are many great mountains in the state of Lu, but Mount Dong alone rises prominently within its borders, drawing the gaze of the whole region. Commanding its territory, it forms a magnificent spectacle for the state. Once Mount Dong has been ascended, a single survey takes in the state, leaving nothing beyond one’s gaze; its hundred-li domain lies almost entirely within view. Mounts Gui and Meng lie to either side: point toward them, and one sees only their lowliness. Mounts Fu and Yi lie before and behind: glance at them, and one senses only their narrowness. Is this because Lu is small? Mount Dong towers far above the state of Lu; viewed from Mount Dong, Lu cannot but seem small. The Way of Confucius is so great that nothing equals it. He merely ascends Mount Dong once and regards Lu as small—who can compare with him?
Did Confucius then ascend Mount Tai? There is no shortage of great mountains under Heaven, but Mount Tai alone surpasses Hua and Dai in eminence [?], standing lofty as the chief of the Five Sacred Peaks. Its height dominates the vast expanse, towering as the great guardian mountain of the Nine Provinces. Once Mount Tai has been ascended, the boundless universe appears minute…

title: 正德五年浙江鄉試錄
text:
於大觀之下輿圖廣博式微於眷注之間荆梁
雍豫舉不足以曠其盈視青冀徐揚舉不足以
盱其駭矚是豈天下之小邪太山之高超乎天
下自太山視之難為其大矣孔子之道大無與
配一登太山而小天下耳孰能彷彿之哉是則
登東山而小魯所處高而視下小登太山而小
天下所處益高而視下益小孟子指是以狀聖
道可謂善於名言者矣嗟夫夫子之道之大孰
不知之孰不能言之然必體驗之精深然後形
===
容之親切故顏淵卓爾之歎發於旣竭吾才之
後子貢天階之喻出於晚年進德之言孟子願
學孔子造道精深故此章反覆形容道體親切
而此二語殆亦發卓爾天階之蘊也歟然則學
者當何如亦曰成章而後達
易
乾元者始而亨者也利貞者性情也
戴顒
同考試官訓導洪批天德妙於萬物聖人指其易
punctuated:
於大觀之下，輿圖廣博，式微於眷注之間。荆梁雍豫，舉不足以曠其盈視；青冀徐揚，舉不足以盱其駭矚。是豈天下之小邪？太山之高超乎天下，自太山視之，難為其大矣。孔子之道大無與配，一登太山而小天下耳，孰能彷彿之哉？是則登東山而小魯，所處高而視下小；登太山而小天下，所處益高而視下益小。孟子指是以狀聖道，可謂善於名言者矣。嗟夫！夫子之道之大，孰不知之？孰不能言之？然必體驗之精深，然後形容之親切。故顏淵卓爾之歎，發於旣竭吾才之後；子貢天階之喻，出於晚年進德之言。孟子願學孔子，造道精深，故此章反覆形容道體親切，而此二語殆亦發卓爾天階之蘊也歟？然則學者當何如？亦曰成章而後達。
易
乾元者，始而亨者也；利貞者，性情也。
戴顒
同考試官訓導洪批：天德妙於萬物，聖人指其易
translation_en:
…beneath that commanding prospect; the vast expanse of the mapped realm dwindles under his gaze. Jing, Liang, Yong, and Yu together cannot fill the breadth of his vision; Qing, Ji, Xu, and Yang together cannot widen his astonished gaze. Does this mean that all under Heaven is small? Mount Tai rises so high above all under Heaven that, viewed from its summit, the world can scarcely seem large. The Way of Confucius is so great that nothing can match it: he merely ascended Mount Tai and found all under Heaven small. Who could approach his likeness? Thus, when he ascended Mount Dong and found Lu small, his position was high and what he looked down upon seemed small; when he ascended Mount Tai and found all under Heaven small, his position was still higher and what he looked down upon seemed smaller still. In pointing to this to describe the sage’s Way, Mencius may indeed be said to have excelled in putting it into words.
Ah! Who does not know the greatness of the Master’s Way? Who cannot speak of it? Yet only after experiencing it with precision and depth can one describe it aptly. Thus Yan Yuan’s sigh over what “stands loftily before me” came after he had “exhausted all my ability”; Zigong’s analogy of ascending Heaven by steps came in words spoken as his virtue advanced in his later years. Mencius aspired to learn from Confucius and attained a profound understanding of the Way. Hence this chapter repeatedly and aptly describes the substance of the Way. Might these two statements also disclose the deeper meaning of “standing loftily” and “steps to Heaven”? What, then, should learners do? Simply this: achieve a complete pattern before advancing further.
Book of Changes
“The primal power of Qian is that which initiates and brings to fulfillment; its power to benefit and remain firm is its inherent nature and disposition.”
Dai Yong
Comment by Associate Examiner Hong, Assistant Instructor: “Heaven’s virtue works wondrously in the myriad things. The sage points to what is easily …”

title: 正德五年浙江鄉試錄
text:
見者以示人學者類多牽合以爲一元統天又於性情
處矜竒發揚說理精到如此篇者絕少
同考試官學正余批乾卦不難於措辭難於精當
得明暢整潔之文若此可與言易矣
考試官學正李批爾雅精密無一長語夫子申釋
彖傳之意瞭然在目
考試官學正張批明爭無疵得易學之體
文言申釋天德有以生物之機言者有以成物
之實言者蓋始而亨者生物之機也性情者成
===
物之實也天德之妙不於是而可見哉文言釋
彖傳之意謂夫維天之命於穆不已觀萬物出
入之機則有以見四德循環之妙矣是故乾之
德始於元而通於亨方其始也靜極而動闔久
而闢化機一啓品彙於是乎權輿元氣一敷萬
有於是乎朕兆權輿者必呈其質而不可遏朕
兆者必流其形而不可禦資始未幾而嘉會之
即至成象未已而效法之隨形生意勃勃無物
不然何其明盛也景象熈熈無地不爾何其光
punctuated:
見者以示人，學者類多牽合，以爲一元統天，又於性情處矜竒發揚。說理精到如此篇者絕少。
同考試官學正余批：乾卦不難於措辭，難於精當。得明暢整潔之文若此，可與言易矣。
考試官學正李批：爾雅精密，無一長語。夫子申釋彖傳之意，瞭然在目。
考試官學正張批：明爭無疵，得易學之體。
文言申釋天德，有以生物之機言者，有以成物之實言者。蓋始而亨者，生物之機也；性情者，成物之實也。天德之妙，不於是而可見哉？文言釋彖傳之意，謂夫維天之命，於穆不已，觀萬物出入之機，則有以見四德循環之妙矣。是故乾之德，始於元而通於亨。方其始也，靜極而動，闔久而闢。化機一啓，品彙於是乎權輿；元氣一敷，萬有於是乎朕兆。權輿者必呈其質而不可遏，朕兆者必流其形而不可禦。資始未幾，而嘉會之即至；成象未已，而效法之隨形。生意勃勃，無物不然，何其明盛也！景象熈熈，無地不爾，何其光
translation_en:
…what is visible, to show it to people. Scholars mostly force connections, taking the single originating principle to encompass Heaven; moreover, when discussing nature and disposition, they parade novel interpretations and elaborate upon them. Essays that explain the principles as precisely and thoroughly as this one are exceedingly rare.

Associate Examiner Yu, Instructor, comments: With the Qian hexagram, the difficulty lies not in phrasing but in precision and aptness. Someone who produces writing as lucid, fluent, orderly, and polished as this is fit to discuss the Changes.

Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: Refined and precise, without a single superfluous phrase. The Master's intention in further explaining the Commentary on the Judgments is plainly before our eyes.

Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: Clear [?] and flawless, it grasps the essential character of the study of the Changes.

The Commentary on the Words of the Text further explains Heaven's virtue, speaking of it sometimes in terms of the workings that generate things and sometimes in terms of the substantive reality that brings things to completion. For beginning and then flourishing constitute the workings that generate things; nature and disposition constitute the substantive reality that brings things to completion. Is not the subtlety of Heaven's virtue visible here? In explaining the meaning of the Commentary on the Judgments, the Commentary on the Words of the Text holds that Heaven's mandate is profound and unceasing. By observing the workings through which the myriad things emerge and withdraw, one can perceive the subtlety of the cyclical succession of the four virtues.

Thus, Qian's virtue begins with origination and proceeds freely through flourishing. At its beginning, stillness reaches its utmost and becomes movement; what has long been closed opens. Once the workings of transformation unfold, the various kinds of beings come into inception; once primordial vital energy spreads, all that exists shows its first signs. What has come into inception must manifest its substance and cannot be checked; what shows its first signs must unfold its form and cannot be restrained. Scarcely have things drawn upon it for their beginnings when their excellent convergence immediately arrives; before the formation of images has ceased, the realization of patterns follows their taking shape. The impulse of life burgeons: there is no thing in which it is not so. How radiant and abundant it is! The scene is full of flourishing harmony: there is no place where it is not so. How its radiance…

title: 正德五年浙江鄉試錄
text:
大也氣至此而動理至此而行此誠之通也仁
之顯也所謂生物之機者如此乾之元亨豈不
可見乎乾之德遂於利而成於貞及其終也動
極而靜闢久而闔隨物成就性命於是乎各正
實理備具太和於是乎保合大化斂於無迹而
孕和胎秀之意存神功隱於無爲而歸根復命
之理寓出震齊巽者泯然而向實役坤說兌者
寂然而實成性之所具堅定可見非復冲漠無
朕之際也情之所寓完固可窺非復块扎無垠
===
之時也理至此而立氣至此而全此誠之復也
用之藏也所謂成物之實者如此乾之利貞又
不可見乎吁萬物生成妙於四德而一本乎天
乾之大也有如是哉大抵理在天地間如環無
端無有止極遠而世代之元會運世近而目前
之瞬息呼吸大而天地小而一塵亦莫不有四
德存焉是豈特生物然哉孔子發明乾之四德
以物之生成言之指其易見者以示人耳體易
君子尚當推其類而求之可也
punctuated: 大也！氣至此而動，理至此而行，此誠之通也，仁之顯也。所謂生物之機者如此，乾之元亨豈不可見乎？乾之德遂於利而成於貞。及其終也，動極而靜，闢久而闔，隨物成就，性命於是乎各正；實理備具，太和於是乎保合。大化斂於無迹，而孕和胎秀之意存；神功隱於無爲，而歸根復命之理寓。出震齊巽者，泯然而向實；役坤說兌者，寂然而實成。性之所具，堅定可見，非復冲漠無朕之際也；情之所寓，完固可窺，非復块扎無垠之時也。理至此而立，氣至此而全，此誠之復也，用之藏也。所謂成物之實者如此，乾之利貞又不可見乎？吁！萬物生成，妙於四德，而一本乎天，乾之大也有如是哉！大抵理在天地間，如環無端，無有止極。遠而世代之元會運世，近而目前之瞬息呼吸，大而天地，小而一塵，亦莫不有四德存焉。是豈特生物然哉？孔子發明乾之四德，以物之生成言之，指其易見者以示人耳。體易君子，尚當推其類而求之可也。
translation_en:
…how vast it is! At this point, vital force moves and principle proceeds: this is the unfolding of sincerity and the manifestation of benevolence. Such is the impulse that generates things. Can we not see in it Qian’s origination and flourishing? Qian’s virtue reaches fulfillment in benefit and completion in constancy. As it reaches its conclusion, movement reaches its utmost and becomes stillness; what has long been open closes. As each thing is brought to completion, its nature and allotted destiny are each set right; substantive principle is fully present, and supreme harmony is preserved in union. The great transformation withdraws without a trace, yet retains the intent to nurture harmony and gestate excellence. Its wondrous efficacy lies hidden in nonaction, yet embodies the principle of returning to the root and restoring the allotted destiny. Those things that emerge in Zhen and are brought into order in Xun quietly move toward fruition; those that labor in Kun and rejoice in Dui silently attain it. What their nature possesses can now be seen as firm and settled: this is no longer the stage of undifferentiated stillness without discernible signs. What their dispositions embody can now be perceived as complete and secure: this is no longer the time of boundless, tangled growth [?]. At this point, principle is established and vital force becomes complete: this is the return of sincerity and the concealment of functioning. Such is the substantive reality that brings things to completion. Can we not also see in it Qian’s benefit and constancy? Ah! The generation and completion of the myriad things work wondrously through the four virtues, yet have their single root in Heaven. Such indeed is the greatness of Qian!

In general, principle between Heaven and Earth is like a ring without an end: it never stops or reaches a limit. Whether in the vast temporal cycles of yuan, hui, yun, and shi, or in the moments and breaths immediately before us; whether in something as great as Heaven and Earth or as small as a speck of dust, the four virtues are invariably present. How could this apply only to the generation of things? In elucidating Qian’s four virtues, Confucius spoke in terms of the generation and completion of things, merely pointing to what is readily visible in order to instruct people. The gentleman who embodies the Changes should further extend these analogies and seek understanding through them.

title: 正德五年浙江鄉試錄
text:
聚而上者謂之升故受之以升
謝元順
同考試官訓導洪批易本潔靜精微之書豈容雜
以浮辭辭愈多而去理愈遠矣此作用卦爻本色語立
講舂容典則非邃於易學者不能是宜錄出
同考試官學正余批序卦義當先講本卦然後畧
入人事數語仍當歸之卦上作者恣意謾說殊戾本旨
此篇組織經文發明題義根理之作也可嘉可嘉
考試官學正李批意完語潔得序卦傳意
===
考試官學正張批得潔淨精微之旨
惟物之上進也有其由故卦之相承也取其義
蓋物之積聚而益高大此上進之所由也然則
萃卦之後而受之以升得無義乎宜夫子傳序
卦而發其蘊也且上兌下坤卦名曰萃萃有聚
之義也而何以謂之升邪蓋天下之物散之則
小合而聚之則積小以成其高大也試以在人
者言之如學必積而後德可崇也今則旁求博
采凡天下事物之理罔不學焉以聚之於一心
punctuated:
聚而上者謂之升，故受之以升。
謝元順
同考試官訓導洪批：易本潔靜精微之書，豈容雜以浮辭？辭愈多，而去理愈遠矣。此作用卦爻本色語立講，舂容典則，非邃於易學者不能，是宜錄出。
同考試官學正余批：序卦義當先講本卦，然後畧入人事數語，仍當歸之卦上。作者恣意謾說，殊戾本旨。此篇組織經文，發明題義，根理之作也。可嘉！可嘉！
考試官學正李批：意完語潔，得序卦傳意。
考試官學正張批：得潔淨精微之旨。
惟物之上進也有其由，故卦之相承也取其義。蓋物之積聚而益高大，此上進之所由也。然則萃卦之後而受之以升，得無義乎？宜夫子傳序卦而發其蘊也。且上兌下坤，卦名曰萃。萃有聚之義也，而何以謂之升邪？蓋天下之物，散之則小，合而聚之，則積小以成其高大也。試以在人者言之，如學必積而後德可崇也。今則旁求博采，凡天下事物之理，罔不學焉，以聚之於一心。
translation_en:
“What gathers and moves upward is called Ascending; therefore Gathering is followed by Ascending.”
Xie Yuanshun
Comment by Associate Examiner Hong, Assistant Instructor: The Changes is fundamentally a book of purity, stillness, subtlety, and profundity. How could it permit the admixture of empty rhetoric? The more such words there are, the farther one departs from principle. This composition develops its exposition in language native to the hexagrams and their lines. Measured, dignified, and well ordered, it could only have been written by someone deeply versed in the study of the Changes. It deserves to be included in the record.
Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, Instructor: In explaining the meaning of the Sequence of the Hexagrams, one should first discuss the hexagram itself, then briefly introduce a few words about human affairs, and finally return to the hexagram. Writers who indulge in careless, unrestrained discussion greatly depart from the original purport. This essay weaves together the words of the classic and elucidates the meaning of the topic. It is a work rooted in principle. Admirable! Admirable!
Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: Complete in meaning and concise in expression, it captures the intent of the Commentary on the Sequence of the Hexagrams.
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: It captures the purport of purity, stillness, subtlety, and profundity.
Since things have a basis for their upward advancement, the succession of hexagrams draws its meaning from this. Things accumulate and gather, becoming ever higher and greater: this is the basis of upward advancement. Thus, when the hexagram Gathering (Cui) is followed by Ascending (Sheng), could this lack significance? It is fitting that the Master should disclose its underlying meaning in his commentary on the sequence of the hexagrams. With Dui above and Kun below, the hexagram is named Gathering. Cui means gathering; but why, then, speak of ascending? Things in the world are small when dispersed. Brought together and gathered, they accumulate from small beginnings to attain height and greatness. Let us discuss this in terms of human affairs. Learning, for example, must accumulate before virtue can be exalted. One now searches widely and gathers broadly, studying without exception the principles of all affairs and things in the world, so as to gather them within a single mind …

title: 正德五年浙江鄉試錄
text:
兼收並蓄凡前言往行之懿必多識焉以蘊之
於一己由是萬理渾融於知至之餘衆善貫通
於真積之久得於心者有日進無疆之勢止諸
躬者有長裕不設之機駸駸乎上達之境矣得
不謂之升乎如人必聚而後業可大也今則顯
其比而無私合天下之心以為心也豈但類聚
而已乎同乎人而無我通天下之志以為志也
豈但財聚而已乎由是朋來盍簪而大有所得
群聚若丘而匪夷所思得衆賢以彙征而行必
===
有尚可以樹不世之奇勳屈群策以協謀而往
必有功可以建非常之偉績巍巍乎高大之業
矣又不謂之升乎夫萃不徒萃萃必至於升升不
不自升升寔原於萃則萃卦之後將受之以困
邪困則窮而非進也將繼之以漸邪漸雖進而
非上也惟升之為卦地中生木有升進之象柔
以時升有上進之義以升而次萃之後則名義
相須截然不可易矣以萃而居升之前則卦序
相因秩然不可紊矣萃升相次其義如此聖人
punctuated:
兼收並蓄，凡前言往行之懿，必多識焉，以蘊之於一己。由是萬理渾融於知至之餘，衆善貫通於真積之久，得於心者有日進無疆之勢，止諸躬者有長裕不設之機，駸駸乎上達之境矣，得不謂之升乎？如人必聚而後業可大也，今則顯其比而無私，合天下之心以為心也，豈但類聚而已乎？同乎人而無我，通天下之志以為志也，豈但財聚而已乎？由是朋來盍簪，而大有所得；群聚若丘，而匪夷所思。得衆賢以彙征，而行必有尚，可以樹不世之奇勳；屈群策以協謀，而往必有功，可以建非常之偉績。巍巍乎高大之業矣，又不謂之升乎？
夫萃不徒萃，萃必至於升；升不不自升，升寔原於萃。則萃卦之後，將受之以困邪？困則窮而非進也。將繼之以漸邪？漸雖進而非上也。惟升之為卦，地中生木，有升進之象；柔以時升，有上進之義。以升而次萃之後，則名義相須，截然不可易矣；以萃而居升之前，則卦序相因，秩然不可紊矣。萃升相次，其義如此，聖人
translation_en:
…Taking everything in and retaining it together, one must acquaint oneself widely with the excellence of past sayings and deeds, storing it within oneself. Thus, once knowledge has reached its fullest extent, the myriad principles merge into a harmonious whole; through long and genuine accumulation, the many forms of goodness become interconnected. What is apprehended in the mind has the momentum of daily, boundless advance; what abides in one's person has the potential for enduring abundance without restriction [?]. One progresses steadily toward a higher understanding. Can this fail to be called Ascending? Similarly, people must gather together before great undertakings can be accomplished. Now one manifests one's bonds with others without selfishness, taking the hearts of all under Heaven as one's own heart. Is this merely a gathering of like kinds? One joins with others without self-centeredness, bringing the aspirations of all under Heaven into communion and making them one's own. Is this merely an accumulation of wealth [?]? Thus friends come together, gathering like hairpins securing the hair, and much is gained; multitudes gather like a mound, beyond ordinary imagining. With many worthy men advancing together, one's actions are sure to win esteem, and extraordinary achievements unmatched in an age can be established. Drawing upon their collective counsel to deliberate together, one's endeavors are sure to succeed, and exceptional accomplishments can be attained. How lofty and great these undertakings are! Again, can this fail to be called Ascending?
Gathering Together does not end in gathering: gathering must lead to Ascending. Ascending does not arise of itself [?]; it truly originates in Gathering Together. Then should the hexagram Gathering Together be followed by Adversity? Adversity means being at an impasse, not advancing. Should it be followed by Gradual Progress? Gradual Progress, though it signifies advance, does not signify upward movement. Only the hexagram Ascending, with wood growing within the earth, presents the image of rising and advancing. The yielding rises in accordance with the time: this conveys the meaning of upward advance. When Ascending follows Gathering Together, their names and meanings require one another, and their positions are definitively unalterable. When Gathering Together stands before Ascending, the sequence of the hexagrams follows an inherent connection, orderly and admitting no confusion. Such is the meaning of Gathering Together and Ascending following one another. The sage…

title: 正德五年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之序卦夫豈苟焉者哉我儀圖之若孔子之志
學以至從心孟子之善信以至聖神堯舜湯武
上下相交而致盛治何莫非由聚而升乎後世
志學之士願治之君觀此當知所從事矣吁一
卦序相承之間而其蘊有如此然則易豈卜筮
之書哉
書
禹拜昌言曰俞
黃懿
===
同考試官訓導方批題不難於遣詞而難於用
事此篇能以本章意組織成文而理亦周至噫得士
如此吾當斂容而拜矣
考試官學正李批禹拜昌言之意能於文字
中發之知子不獨工於文者也
考試官學正張批文理平正得作經義體
聖人之於同列也既敬受其所言復深然其所
言甚矣善言之足以感人也然非既拜而俞亦
何以見受之敬然之深哉聖人能然宜乎史臣
punctuated:
之序卦，夫豈苟焉者哉！我儀圖之：若孔子之志學以至從心，孟子之善信以至聖神，堯舜湯武上下相交而致盛治，何莫非由聚而升乎？後世志學之士、願治之君，觀此當知所從事矣。吁！一卦序相承之間，而其蘊有如此，然則易豈卜筮之書哉！
書
禹拜昌言，曰：「俞。」
黃懿
同考試官訓導方批：題不難於遣詞，而難於用事。此篇能以本章意組織成文，而理亦周至。噫！得士如此，吾當斂容而拜矣。
考試官學正李批：禹拜昌言之意，能於文字中發之，知子不獨工於文者也。
考試官學正張批：文理平正，得作經義體。
聖人之於同列也，既敬受其所言，復深然其所言。甚矣，善言之足以感人也！然非既拜而俞，亦何以見受之敬、然之深哉？聖人能然，宜乎史臣
translation_en:
…in arranging the hexagrams, how could the sage have acted arbitrarily? As I consider this [?], take Confucius’s progress from setting his heart on learning to following his heart’s desires, or Mencius’s progression from goodness and genuineness to sagehood and spiritual perfection, or Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wu bringing about flourishing government through interaction between those above and below: which of these did not proceed from gathering to ascending? Scholars of later ages intent on learning, and rulers desirous of good government, should recognize from this what they ought to pursue. Ah! Such implications lie within the succession of just these hexagrams. Can the Book of Changes, then, be merely a book of divination?

Book of Documents
“Yu bowed at these excellent words and said, ‘Yes.’”
Huang Yi

Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, Assistant Instructor: The difficulty of this topic lies not in wording but in deploying the relevant events. This essay weaves the meaning of the original chapter into a composition whose reasoning is also comprehensive and thorough. Ah! On finding a scholar such as this, I ought to compose my countenance respectfully and bow.

Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: You have succeeded in expressing through your writing the meaning of Yu’s bowing at these excellent words. I can tell that your accomplishments extend beyond literary skill alone.

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: The writing and reasoning are balanced and sound, conforming to the proper form for an exposition of a classic’s meaning.

In his dealings with his peers, the sage both respectfully received what they said and profoundly assented to it. How powerfully good words can move a person! Yet, had he not both bowed and said ‘Yes,’ how could the respect with which he received them and the depth of his assent have been shown? Since the sage could act thus, it was fitting that the court historian…

title: 正德五年浙江鄉試錄
text:
有以紀之也昔大禹奉辭伐苗聞伯益賛佐之
言而有所感故稱其言爲昌言而拜之其心以
爲言焉無稽所見或泥於泛常而非昌言矣益
乃諄諄乎惟德是脩而不及於動兵誠爲盛德
之言聞之而不拜何以展其敬邪言焉遜志所
陳或習於比昵而非德言矣益乃亹亹乎惟内
之治而不事乎外攘實爲盛德之言得之而不
拜何以答其意邪因外以感乎中斂容而拜不
以時方用武而忽禮於倉卒之間由中以達於
===
外鞠躬而拜不以身居既攝而忘情於僚寀之
舊所以然者非過恭也受善之敬一發於中之
存耳豈惟是哉禹於是又謂苗之逆命固當往
征然動兵不如脩德汝之所言深有以契我心
之同然豈泛常而爲無稽之言乎苗之弗率固
當致討然内治切於外攘汝之所論良有以資
今日之治道豈比昵而爲遜志之言乎反覆於
中汝之所陳鑿乎其有見若果於理不合我亦
不以倉卒之故不之咈而俞也體驗於事汝之
punctuated: 有以紀之也。昔大禹奉辭伐苗，聞伯益賛佐之言而有所感，故稱其言爲昌言而拜之。其心以爲：言焉無稽，所見或泥於泛常，而非昌言矣。益乃諄諄乎惟德是脩，而不及於動兵，誠爲盛德之言，聞之而不拜，何以展其敬邪？言焉遜志，所陳或習於比昵，而非德言矣。益乃亹亹乎惟内之治，而不事乎外攘，實爲盛德之言，得之而不拜，何以答其意邪？因外以感乎中，斂容而拜，不以時方用武而忽禮於倉卒之間；由中以達於外，鞠躬而拜，不以身居既攝而忘情於僚寀之舊。所以然者，非過恭也，受善之敬，一發於中之存耳。豈惟是哉？禹於是又謂：苗之逆命，固當往征，然動兵不如脩德。汝之所言，深有以契我心之同然，豈泛常而爲無稽之言乎？苗之弗率，固當致討，然内治切於外攘。汝之所論，良有以資今日之治道，豈比昵而爲遜志之言乎？反覆於中，汝之所陳，鑿乎其有見。若果於理不合，我亦不以倉卒之故，不之咈而俞也。體驗於事，汝之
translation_en:
…had grounds to record it.

Formerly, when the Great Yu undertook the expedition against the Miao under sovereign command, he was moved by Bo Yi’s words of counsel and assistance. He therefore called them excellent words and bowed to him. In his heart he thought: Words without foundation may express views confined to commonplace notions; these would not be excellent words. Yet Yi earnestly urged only the cultivation of virtue, without advocating military action. These were truly words of abundant virtue. If I heard them without bowing, how could I express my respect? Words that accord with one’s wishes may merely repeat the language of ingratiating familiarity; these would not be virtuous words. Yet Yi tirelessly urged only the ordering of affairs within, without pursuing the repulsion of enemies abroad. These were indeed words of abundant virtue. If I received them without bowing, how could I respond to his intentions?

Moved inwardly by what came from without, Yu composed his countenance and bowed. He did not neglect ritual propriety amid the urgency of the moment merely because he was engaged in warfare. Giving outward expression to what was within, he bent his body and bowed. He did not forget his affection for an old colleague merely because he now occupied the position of regent [?]. His doing so was no excessive display of deference: the respect with which he received good counsel arose entirely from what he held within his heart.

Was this all? Yu then further said: The Miao’s defiance of the command certainly warrants an expedition against them, yet taking up arms is inferior to cultivating virtue. Your words deeply accord with what my own heart recognizes as right. How could they be mere commonplaces, words without foundation? The Miao’s refusal to obey certainly warrants punishment, yet ordering affairs within is more pressing than repelling enemies abroad. What you have argued truly contributes to the proper way of governing today. How could it be ingratiating familiarity, words that merely accord with my wishes? Turning it over repeatedly in my heart, I find that what you have presented assuredly shows insight. If it really failed to accord with principle, I would not, merely because of the urgency of the moment, refrain from rejecting it and instead assent. Testing it against affairs, what you…

title: 正德五年浙江鄉試錄
text:
所論信乎其可行苟或於道有違我亦不以僚
寀之故不之吁而俞也所以然者非尚同也稱
善之誠一本乎心之發耳吁聖人樂善之心如
此蓋能視人猶己公天下以為心者也有苗安
能不來格於班師之後哉大抵虞廷君臣一德
相與以成大業者也故禹聞益賛而整旅以還
舜於其時而誕敷文德上下體悉蕩蕩然如天
地之覆幬無一物不在其中蠢兹有苗順逆奚
足較哉然干羽之舞未畢而來格之化已行蓋
===
未有誠而不動者也聖人亦何容心之有數千
載之下讀其書猶可以想其一時之氣象
天休滋至惟時二人弗戡其汝克敬德明
我俊民在讓後人于丕時嗚呼篤棐時二
人我式克至于今日休我咸成文王功于
不怠丕冒海隅出日罔不率俾公曰君予
不惠若茲多誥予惟用閔于天越民公曰
嗚呼君惟乃知民德亦罔不能厥初惟其
終祗若茲往敬用治
punctuated:
所論信乎其可行，苟或於道有違，我亦不以僚寀之故不之吁而俞也。所以然者，非尚同也，稱善之誠一本乎心之發耳。吁！聖人樂善之心如此，蓋能視人猶己，公天下以為心者也。有苗安能不來格於班師之後哉？大抵虞廷君臣一德，相與以成大業者也。故禹聞益賛而整旅以還，舜於其時而誕敷文德，上下體悉，蕩蕩然如天地之覆幬，無一物不在其中。蠢兹有苗，順逆奚足較哉？然干羽之舞未畢，而來格之化已行，蓋未有誠而不動者也。聖人亦何容心之有？數千載之下，讀其書，猶可以想其一時之氣象。

天休滋至，惟時二人弗戡。其汝克敬德，明我俊民，在讓後人于丕時。嗚呼！篤棐時二人，我式克至于今日休。我咸成文王功于不怠，丕冒海隅出日，罔不率俾。公曰：「君，予不惠，若茲多誥，予惟用閔于天越民。」公曰：「嗚呼！君惟乃知民德，亦罔不能厥初，惟其終。祗若茲，往敬用治。」
translation_en:
…what you have proposed is indeed practicable. If it should run counter to the Way, I would not, merely because we are fellow officials, withhold my dissent and assent to it instead. My reason for doing so is not a preference for agreement: my sincerity in commending what is good springs entirely from the heart.” Ah! Such is the sage’s delight in goodness. He regards others as himself and takes the impartial good of all under Heaven as his own concern. How could the Youmiao fail to come into submission after the army’s return?

The ruler and ministers at the court of Yu were united in virtue and worked together to accomplish their great undertaking. Thus, when Yu heard Yi’s counsel, he marshalled his troops and returned; Shun then spread the transforming influence of civil virtue far and wide. Those above and below fully embodied it, its vast reach resembling the sheltering embrace of Heaven and Earth, with not a single thing excluded. What need was there to reckon whether these unruly Youmiao were obedient or rebellious? Before the dance with shields and feathers was finished, its transforming influence had already brought them into submission. For sincerity has never failed to move others. What deliberate calculation could the sage have had? Thousands of years later, reading this account, we can still imagine the spirit of that time.

“Heaven’s blessings came in growing abundance, but these two men could not sustain them. May you reverently cultivate virtue, bring our outstanding men to light, and pass on this great opportunity to those who come after. Ah! Give steadfast support to these two men, so that we may attain the blessings of this day. Let us together complete King Wen’s achievement without slackening, extending its shelter far to the seacoasts and the sunrise, so that none fail to obey.”

The Duke said: “My lord, I am not wise, yet I offer so many admonitions as these. I do so only out of concern for Heaven and the people.”

The Duke said: “Ah! My lord, you know that in the people’s practice of virtue, none are incapable of making a beginning; it is the ending that matters. Reverently follow these words. Go, and govern with reverence.”

title: 正德五年浙江鄉試錄
text:
柴經
同考試官訓導方批作長題文字雖貴收拾然詞
滯理晦亦在所忌此篇敘事不遺行文有則而於當緩
急處言之略不費力殆邃於壁經者歟
考試官學正李批善言周召二公之心故錄之
考試官學正張批此題作者類能言之長者傷
於繁短者失其意甚至天命民心亦全體認不明此篇
依經為文詞理兩得故取之以冠本房
聖臣歷敘天民之當重也其辭詳推言民心之
===
尤重也其意切蓋天命民心實惟在人而民心
又天命之本聖臣以是為言何其忠愛之至哉
昔召公告老而去周公留之意謂我欲公留之
意固已陳夫往跡尚未遡其所由是故以天命
言之天眷我周方有滋至之美是我二人將有
不勝之憂汝若以盈滿為懼也則當能自敬德
益加寅畏于以明揚俊民布列於庶位國斯有
人而時臻盛大汝乃肥遯而遜諸後人是或可
也今天休未答豈可以言歸乎以民心言之篤
punctuated:
柴經

同考試官訓導方批：作長題文字，雖貴收拾，然詞滯理晦，亦在所忌。此篇敘事不遺，行文有則，而於當緩急處，言之略不費力，殆邃於壁經者歟？

考試官學正李批：善言周召二公之心，故錄之。

考試官學正張批：此題作者類能言之，長者傷於繁，短者失其意，甚至天命民心亦全體認不明。此篇依經為文，詞理兩得，故取之以冠本房。

聖臣歷敘天民之當重也，其辭詳；推言民心之尤重也，其意切。蓋天命民心，實惟在人，而民心又天命之本。聖臣以是為言，何其忠愛之至哉！

昔召公告老而去，周公留之，意謂：我欲公留之意，固已陳夫往跡，尚未遡其所由。是故以天命言之，天眷我周，方有滋至之美，是我二人將有不勝之憂。汝若以盈滿為懼也，則當能自敬德，益加寅畏，于以明揚俊民，布列於庶位。國斯有人，而時臻盛大，汝乃肥遯而遜諸後人，是或可也。今天休未答，豈可以言歸乎？以民心言之，篤
translation_en:
Chai Jing 柴經

Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, Assistant Instructor: In writing on a long examination topic, bringing the material together is valued, but cumbersome wording and obscure reasoning must also be avoided. This essay omits nothing in recounting events and proceeds in an orderly manner. Where the pace should slacken or quicken, its expression is entirely effortless. Might its author be deeply versed in the “Wall Classic” [?]?

Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: It expresses well the intentions of the two dukes, Zhou and Shao; therefore I have selected it.

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: Those writing on this topic can generally discuss it, but the longer essays suffer from prolixity, while the shorter ones lose its meaning. Some even fail altogether to grasp Heaven’s mandate and the people’s allegiance. This essay follows the Classic in its composition and succeeds in both expression and reasoning. I have therefore selected it to rank first in this examining section.

When the sagely minister enumerates why Heaven and the people must be held in reverence, his language is detailed; when he develops the point that the people’s allegiance deserves particular weight, his meaning is earnest. For Heaven’s mandate and the people’s allegiance truly depend upon human action, and the people’s allegiance is itself the foundation of Heaven’s mandate.
